范明明老师实验室.title: Beyond Appearance Shifts: Task-Semantic Action Calibration for VLA Models
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Shuaijun Liu, Feiyang You, Chengyu Wu, Shuyang Hao, Chenglong Zhang
范明明老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces BAS-VLA, a framework enhancing VLA models' performance by calibrating actions based on task semantics, addressing issues of action drift and behavioral distinctiveness.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong performance in embodied manipulation, but still lack a clear mechanism to balance behavioral stability with task-semantic sensitivity. We identify two complementary failure modes. Under task-preserving changes, where task semantics remain unchanged but scene appearance varies (e.g., style, illumination, clutter, or paraphrasing), policies often exhibit unnecessary action drift. Conversely, under semantic-breaking changes, where key task semantics such as the target object or constraint are altered, policies frequently fail to produce sufficiently distinct behaviors and instead follow the original trajectory. To address this gap, we propose BAS-VLA, a task-semantic action calibration framework built on top of a frozen base VLA. BAS-VLA adopts a breaking-centered calibration core as the default path, and introduces a selective evidence-gated preserving auxiliary that activates only when nuisance variation is detected while task semantics remain consistent. On the OpenPI-pi0.5 / LIBERO-Object Milk-Swap benchmark, BAS-VLA maintains high success on clean (98.0%) and semantics-preserving conditions (97.5%), while reducing clean-criterion success to 0.0% under deliberate target-object swaps, demonstrating strong stale-task suppression and task-semantic separation. On validated style-preserving shifts, it improves success from 42% to 70% without degrading clean performance. These results highlight that reliable VLA behavior requires moving beyond appearance robustness toward explicit task-semantic action calibration.

范明明老师实验室.title: SalQ-VLM: Fine-Grained Saliency-Guided Quantization for Vision-Language Models
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yufei Xue, Yushi Huang, Lunjie Zhu, Jiawei Shao, Jun Zhang
范明明老师实验室.summary: SalQ-VLM introduces a saliency-guided quantization framework for vision-language models, enhancing performance by prioritizing important tokens and reducing redundancy without additional inference costs.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across diverse language tasks, motivating their extension to vision-language models (VLMs) for multimodal understanding. However, billion-parameter VLMs incur substantial memory and computational costs that hinder deployment in resource-constrained settings. Post-training quantization (PTQ) compresses models and accelerates inference without retraining, yet remains underexplored for VLMs. We identify two intrinsic VLM activation properties in PTQ: (1) visual over-representation, where vision tokens are excessive and often redundant, and (2) the modality gap separating text and vision tokens in the latent feature space. Prior methods largely overlook these properties, leading to quantization performance degradation. To address this mismatch, we propose SalQ-VLM, an importance-aware PTQ framework that prioritizes salient tokens and suppresses redundant vision tokens during calibration. We derive a gradient-driven importance factor that captures token-level importance variance and is theoretically grounded in the relationship among loss perturbation, activation errors, and output gradients. SalQ-VLM obtains this factor through a single lightweight block-wise gradient-caching pass and incorporates it into the layer-wise reconstruction objective. Because SalQ-VLM modifies only calibration, it adds no inference-time operations and remains compatible with existing high-performance kernels. Extensive evaluations across benchmarks and backbones show that SalQ-VLM consistently outperforms strong PTQ baselines, especially under ultra-low-bit quantization. Notably, it improves MME-RealWorld accuracy by 16.45% under INT2g128 quantization.

范明明老师实验室.title: OnlineWM: Causality-Aware Active Online Learning for Effective World Modeling
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yikun Miao, Fangqi Zhu, Quanxin Shou, Xiaoyi Pang, Zhengyang Yan
范明明老师实验室.summary: OnlineWM is an innovative online learning framework that enhances world modeling by actively querying simulators and employing causality-aware optimization to improve predictive accuracy and robustness.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Generative world models aim to predict future states conditioned on actions, where action controllability is fundamental for reliable dynamics modeling. While recent efforts leverage simulator-generated data to enhance this capability, existing training pipelines face two fundamental limitations. First, static offline data collection leads to a distribution misalignment between training sets and the model's evolving error patterns, failing to resolve critical long-tail scenarios where dynamics predictions remain unreliable. Second, the standard objective of minimizing observational discrepancy often encourages the model to exploit spurious correlations instead of capturing the underlying action-effect causality. To address these limitations, we propose OnlineWM, an online training framework that continuously improves world modeling through active simulator interaction and causality-aware optimization. OnlineWM introduces two key innovations: (1) Active Online Learning: Instead of using fixed datasets, OnlineWM adaptively queries the simulator for new interaction sequences that target the model's current predictive weaknesses, ensuring high-utility data acquisition. (2) Causality-Aware Fine-Tuning: We propose a counterfactual learning strategy that contrasts the outcomes of different actions from identical states, forcing the model to attribute state transitions to specific actions rather than ambient environmental evolution, thereby grounding its predictions in reliable causal mechanisms. By integrating active data acquisition with causal optimization, OnlineWM establishes a closed-loop refinement process that ensures the model is both robust to diverse scenarios and precise in its causal attribution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OnlineWM significantly enhances action controllability and generalizes effectively to unseen domains.

范明明老师实验室.title: Data Agents: Agentic Data Systems
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Guoliang Li, Peiyao Zhou, Xuanhe Zhou, Ji Sun, Yuyu Luo
范明明老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces Data Agents, autonomous systems that enhance data management and analysis by shifting from manual processes to proactive, semantic-driven orchestration.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Traditional data systems face profound limitations in the AI era, relying on human-crafted pipelines, lacking semantic understanding of heterogeneous data, and operating through rigid, reactive processing. To address these challenges, we propose a new paradigm called the Data Agent, designed to manage, process, and analyze data with minimal human intervention. Data agents autonomously execute a wide range of data-related tasks, transforming traditional data systems by shifting from manual design to autonomous orchestration, from literal manipulation to semantic interpretation, and from reactive to proactive processing. Our Data Agent system includes six components: semantic data organization, semantic operators, agentic pipeline orchestration and optimization, feedback-driven refinement, memory management, and proactive adaptation. Building on this foundation, we also develop two specialized agents: the data analytics agent and the data science agent. Experiments on real benchmarks demonstrate significant performance gains of our data agent over state-of-the-art methods. We identify open challenges to guide future research in building fully autonomous data systems.

范明明老师实验室.title: GraspTune: Tactile-Driven Execution Refinement for Robust Grasping
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Juntao Li, Xingke Xia, Sichao Liu, Daqiang Guo
范明明老师实验室.summary: GraspTune enhances grasp stability by refining visual proposals with tactile feedback, achieving significant success rate improvements across simulated and real-robot trials.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Visual grasp proposal generation has advanced rapidly, yet converting a selected proposal into a stable physical grasp remains a central execution-stage challenge. This paper introduces GraspTune, a tactile-driven execution-stage refinement framework that starts from a nominal proposal and applies bounded residual TCP motions during approach, contact formation, and final grasp execution. GraspTune learns control-facing contact semantics from local depth, tactile signals, state, and history using state-conditioned expert contact queries and multi-task supervision for contact change, contact risk, and post-close readiness. The representation conditions a diffusion-pretrained residual policy and is aligned with PPO for closed-loop execution. Across more than 60,000 simulated executions over 20 object categories, GraspTune establishes an execution-layer benefit across four proposal generators, raising stable grasp success by +19.22, +9.55, +12.45, and +20.70 percentage points for GraspNet, Contact-GraspNet, AnyGrasp, and VGN. A four-fold held-out category study raises unseen-object execution from 54.58% to 70.33%, showing category-disjoint generalization of contact correction. Across more than 1,000 real-robot trials on a UR5e setup with Xense fingertip sensors, GraspTune raises GraspNet execution from 71.0% to 84.3%, validating direct transfer without realworld policy fine-tuning. Together, these results turn visually plausible proposals into stable physical grasps for downstream contact-rich manipulation. A supplementary video is available at https://youtu.be/kcq7fSLNtzU.

范明明老师实验室.title: A Topological Representation with Object-Path Graphs for Open-Vocabulary Instance Navigation
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Linwei Zheng, Daojie Peng, Bingtao Wang, Haoang Li, Jun Ma
范明明老师实验室.summary: This paper presents an object-path graph for integrating open-vocabulary semantic reasoning with topological navigation, enhancing navigation efficiency without dense metric maps.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language navigation requires embodied agents to navigate environments using natural language instructions and visual observations. Existing approaches typically decompose navigation into sequential language-guided decisions or rely on online exploration without prior environmental knowledge. Scene graph representations offer compact semantic memory but remain decoupled from downstream navigation, which still depends on dense metric maps. To close this gap, we propose an object--path graph that unifies open-vocabulary semantic reasoning with topological navigation. The proposed representation jointly supports semantic grounding, graph-based localization, and navigation within a single lightweight topological framework. Building on this graph, we introduce a navigation strategy that combines global path planning with local inter-node execution through lightweight node localization and semantic visual servoing, enabling navigation directly over the graph without dense metric reconstruction. Experiments on HM3D and Replica demonstrate competitive performance in open-vocabulary object grounding through the proposed hierarchical graph structure, while achieving effective navigation performance. Real-world robot experiments further validate the practicality of the proposed framework.

范明明老师实验室.title: MoE-ACT: Scaling Multi-Task Bimanual Manipulation with Sparse Task-Conditioned Mixture-of-Experts Transformers
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Kangjun Guo, Haichao Liu, Yanji Sun, Ruhan Zhao, Jinni Zhou
范明明老师实验室.summary: MoE-ACT introduces a parameter-efficient multi-task framework for bimanual manipulation, achieving superior performance and efficiency by leveraging sparse Mixture-of-Experts Transformers.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Developing a unified policy for multi-task robotic manipulation remains challenging due to policy degradation from task interference and negative transfer. In this work, we propose Mixture-of-Experts-Enhanced Action Chunking Transformer (MoE-ACT), a parameter-efficient multi-task visuomotor framework tailored for bimanual manipulation. MoE-ACT incorporates sparse MoE layers into the ACT encoder, dynamically routing image tokens to selected experts based on task context, visual observations, and proprioceptive states. Furthermore, the framework incorporates task-conditioned Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) in the action decoder alongside multi-scale cross-attention, ensuring precise task grounding and capturing fine-grained spatial cues. Extensive evaluations on the RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark across 16 challenging bimanual tasks demonstrate that MoE-ACT achieves an average success rate of 62.0%, outperforming standard ACT by 17.4 percentage points. Crucially, with only 195M activated parameters, MoE-ACT surpasses the 16-fold larger foundation model $π$0 (3.24B) by 5.1 percentage points, exhibiting substantial gains in parameter efficiency and deployment feasibility. Real-robot dual-arm experiments consistently confirm its superior multi-task execution capabilities. Our open-source project page can be found at https://j3k7.github.io/MoE-ACT/.

范明明老师实验室.title: D-JEPA: A Decision-Aligned Latent World Model
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Shuaijun Liu, Chengyu Wu, Qifu Wen, Feiyang You, Chenglong Zhang
范明明老师实验室.summary: D-JEPA enhances latent world models by aligning decision-relevant relations with executed outcomes, improving action selection in robotics and autonomous systems across various tasks.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Latent world models predict the consequences of actions, but accurate prediction does not guarantee that latent distance reflects which candidate will execute successfully. We identify a decision-local prediction gap: among the few futures competing for execution, a candidate predicted closer to the goal can produce a worse realized outcome than an available alternative. We introduce D-JEPA, a decision-aligned latent world model that learns decision-relevant relations among candidate futures from executed outcomes. A bounded, permutation-equivariant operator jointly reasons over goal-relative predictive features and ordinal evidence, refining pretrained predictive geometry where action choices are most consequential. Restricted predictor adaptation and a shared ordinal interface extend this alignment across complementary predictive geometries. D-JEPA further realizes the learned decision structure in JEPA-compatible future representations, enabling deployment through native latent-distance planning. Evaluations across latent control, manipulation, pretrained action-producing models, physical robots and autonomous driving demonstrate improved action selection, including 87.89% success on PushT, a 15.04-point average gain on RoboTwin, and a 17-point gain on physical robot tasks. These results establish decision-relevant relational structure as a direct bridge between predictive world modeling and effective control.

范明明老师实验室.title: GAE: Learning a Geometry-Native Latent Space for 3D-Consistent World Generation
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Jiahao Lu, Minghao Yin, Wenbo Hu, Hengyu Liu, Wang Zhao
范明明老师实验室.summary: The GAE introduces a geometry-native latent space that enhances 3D-consistent world generation, improving visual quality and coherence in generated scenes.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: We present a compact geometry-native latent space as a shared foundation for perception and generation. Visual generators can produce photorealistic frames without preserving a consistent 3D scene. We argue that this is not only a modeling problem but also a representation problem: generators typically evolve appearance-centric latents, while perception models recover geometry in a semantically rich space that encodes cross-view structure. Rather than adding geometry as another output, we reparameterize a geometry foundation model's features into a compact latent space for generation. We realize this shift with the geometry-native autoencoder (GAE), whose latent is jointly decodable to appearance, depth, cameras, and point maps. With this state, a standard conditional flow supports diverse generation tasks. In controlled comparisons that hold the generator and training protocol fixed, replacing the latent with GAE improves both visual quality and independently measured 3D coherence: FVD falls by $12.7\%$ and $23.1\%$ on RealEstate10K and DL3DV, and camera-trajectory error is halved on RealEstate10K. Together, these results show that the latent space is central to geometry-consistent generation and can serve as a shared interface between perception and generation.

范明明老师实验室.title: ForceRFT: Refining VLA Actions through Force-Guided Residual Reinforcement Learning
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yichen Wang, Chaoyang Zhang, Xuqi Su, Jun Ma, Haiyue Zhu
范明明老师实验室.summary: ForceRFT enhances VLA policies by integrating force-guided residual reinforcement learning with human corrections and autonomous outcomes, improving task success rates in real-robot applications.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Force-conditioned vision-language-action (VLA) policies can respond to contact, but when trained solely on demonstrations, their recovery behavior may be limited by demonstration coverage, and they do not learn from deployment outcomes. Human corrective imitation provides additional recovery examples, but its objective matches local action targets without explicitly optimizing task return. We present ForceRFT, a force-guided residual reinforcement learning framework that learns contact-dependent corrections from human supervision and autonomous task outcomes. A frozen, demonstration-trained SmolVLA-based prior generates force-conditioned action chunks, while a lightweight residual actor refines individual end-effector pose commands using wrist feedback acquired during chunk execution. The decision-time wrist wrench, its temporal change, and the selected base motion condition both residual correction and value estimation. Human corrections supervise the residual actor, while verified autonomous transitions train the twin critics and support value-guided updates to the same actor. Bootstrapping is restricted to autonomous segments, preventing TD credit from crossing human-intervention boundaries. Real-robot experiments on plug insertion, ring-on-peg assembly, and whiteboard wiping show higher autonomous success rates than the evaluated demonstration-trained and residual-imitation baselines. Comparisons with residual imitation support value-guided residual optimization, while plug-insertion ablations indicate the benefit of direct execution-time wrist feedback.

范明明老师实验室.title: Connect the Dots: Training LLMs for Long-Lifecycle Agents with Cross-Domain Generalization Via Reinforcement Learning
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yanxi Chen, Weijie Shi, Boyi Hu, Zeyue Zhang, Zhiwei Wang
范明明老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces a framework for training LLMs to enhance long-lifecycle agents' performance through reinforcement learning, enabling cross-domain generalization and iterative self-updating capabilities.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: This work presents a general framework for training large language models (LLMs) to "Connect the Dots" (CoD), a meta-capability required by long-lifecycle agents: as an LLM-based AI agent gets deployed in an environment, it solves a long sequence of tasks while continuously exploring the environment, learning from its own experiences, and iteratively self-updating its context about the environment, thereby achieving progressively better performance on future tasks conditioned on the updated context. Major components of the CoD framework include: (1) algorithm design and infrastructure for end-to-end reinforcement learning (RL) with long rollout sequences interleaving solve-task and update-context episodes; (2) tasks and environments for incentivizing and eliciting the targeted meta-capability in LLMs during training, as well as for faithfully measuring progress during evaluation. We present proof-of-concept implementations of the CoD framework, including a GRPO-style RL algorithm with fine-grained credit assignment, as well as tasks and environments tailored to the targeted meta-capability (rather than domain-specific LLM capabilities or standard task-by-task RL). Empirical results with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3.6-27B validate the efficacy of end-to-end RL training in the CoD setting, and demonstrate the potential for out-of-distribution generalization -- within the training domains, across different domains, and from CoD to Ralph-loop settings -- of the elicited meta-capability. Our investigation of CoD connects several lines of prior work, and opens up new opportunities for advancing LLMs and AI agents. To facilitate further research and applications, we release our implementations at https://github.com/agentscope-ai/Trinity-RFT/tree/research/cod_v2/examples/research_cod.

范明明老师实验室.title: BiRoAD: Learning Shared and Role-Adaptive Representations for Bimanual Manipulation
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yan Shen, Yuchen Liu, Feng Jiang, Hangtian Hu, Xiaoqi Li
范明明老师实验室.summary: BiRoAD introduces a framework for learning adaptive bimanual manipulation policies that enhance robustness by decomposing actions into role-invariant and role-specific components, improving generalization across diverse tasks.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Bimanual manipulation requires policies that coordinate two arms while adapting their functional roles to scene geometry, object configuration, and task context. Learning such scene-conditioned role adaptation remains challenging, as demonstrations may contain uneven role distributions that limit generalization to underrepresented arm--role configurations. In addition, many bimanual policies predict actions in fixed left- and right-arm action spaces. While this provides a natural parameterization for robot control, it does not explicitly specify how behaviors should transform when functional roles are exchanged across arms. Across different scene initializations, the two arms may follow a similar coordination pattern, but the role-specific behavior assigned to each arm should change with the scene. Therefore, we propose BiRoAD, a Bimanual Role-Adaptive Decomposition framework for learning shared and role-adaptive representations in bimanual policies. Given bimanual trajectory or action-token features, BiRoAD decomposes these features into swap--symmetric and swap--antisymmetric components: the former captures coordination structure invariant to arm exchange, and the latter captures role-specific distinctions that vary consistently with functional role assignment. The two components are then recomposed as residual updates to the original paired arm representations, allowing BiRoAD to serve as a modular feature transformation without changing the policy inputs, imitation-learning objective, or requiring manually defined role labels. Across multiple bimanual manipulation tasks with balanced and imbalanced role distributions, BiRoAD improves robustness across role configurations over corresponding base policies, with notable gains on underrepresented role configurations.

范明明老师实验室.title: MoSAT: Human Motion Generation from Spatial Audio and Textual Description
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Shuyang Xu, Zhiyang Dou, Yiduo Hao, Zekun Li, Liang Pan
范明明老师实验室.summary: The paper presents MoSAT, a framework for generating human motion from spatial audio and textual descriptions, achieving state-of-the-art performance through hierarchical cross-attention and a novel dataset.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Human motion is shaped by both external acoustic events and behavioral intent: spatial audio conveys environmental cues that elicit or guide a response, while text specifies the desired action and how it should be performed. In this paper, we study the novel task of human motion synthesis jointly conditioned on spatial audio and natural language, a problem that has been largely overlooked in previous research. To support this task, We introduce STAM, a dataset of motion sequences paired with spatial audio and detailed textual annotations whose rich vocabulary affords precise and nuanced specification of human motions. We further introduce MoSAT, a latent flow-matching framework for full-body motion generation jointly conditioned on natural-language intent and directional spatial-audio cues through hierarchical cross-attention before generating motion. Such a hierarchical design enhances temporally coherent and semantically aligned motion sequences. We also develop tri-modal evaluators for comprehensive evaluation on this novel task. Extensive experiments show that MoSAT achieves the SOTA performance by leveraging spatial audio's intrinsic motion-shaping properties alongside textual semantics, enabling precise and diverse motion in various scenarios.

范明明老师实验室.title: WidgetVA: A Widget-Centric Framework and Benchmark for Agentic Visual Analytics
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yutong Chen, Zhike Tang, Zhihao Mai, Zhihao Shuai, Danli Luo
范明明老师实验室.summary: WidgetVA introduces a standardized framework and benchmark for autonomous visual analytics, enabling agents to efficiently interact with and analyze data through structured widgets.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Visual analytics (VA) enables sensemaking through interactive visualization, but effective analysis often requires experts to translate high-level intents into long sequences of interface operations and iteratively interpret visual feedback. We study whether modern vision-language models (VLMs) can take on this role as autonomous VA operators that observe the interface, plan multi-step exploration, execute interactions, and adapt based on intermediate visual feedback. To support systematic development and evaluation, we first introduce WidgetVA, a widget-centric agentic VA framework that standardizes interactive components as structured widgets with unified action (e.g., filter and zoom) and perception-query (e.g., selection summaries) APIs. This standardization supports two modes of system construction: wrapping an existing VA system to make it agent-operable without rebuilding it, and composing a new system from widgets as modular building blocks. To help agents coordinate across widgets rather than plan each interaction from scratch, each widget further packages reusable analytical workflows, giving agents more than a bare set of callable functions to plan over. Building on this framework, we present WidgetVABench, a benchmark of single- and multi-widget VA tasks that require agents to perform multi-step interactions to uncover evidence and produce verifiable results. Each task also provides fine-grained reference annotations so that WidgetVABench can score Answer, Reference Trace Similarity, and State separately rather than collapsing agent performance into one success score. Experiments across multiple VLMs show that our framework provides an effective scaffold for agentic VA, while the diagnostic measures expose persistent limitations for future work. The WidgetVA framework and WidgetVABench have been released in https://github.com/Hiverwin/widgetva.

范明明老师实验室.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Haoran Ye, Yuxing Lu, Haonan Dong, Zhaochen Su, Guojie Song
范明明老师实验室.summary: Harness-Zero enables effective agent harness distillation by using an optimized harness to guide training, enhancing model performance and behavior recovery without requiring specialized harnesses at deployment.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the harness at deployment. Because the best harness varies across domains, instances, and models, a general-purpose agent must either settle for a suboptimal shared harness or route among an ever-growing set of specialized ones. We therefore study agent harness distillation: using a domain- or instance-optimized harness as training-time guidance and transferring the behaviors it induces into model weights, so that its gains survive under a single fixed target harness. The challenge is that the two harnesses differ in action space and available information, so guidance from the optimized harness cannot serve directly as supervision for the target one. We introduce Harness-Zero, which enables harness distillation through agent-as-harness. Guided by the optimized harness, a harnessing agent corrects student responses before execution in the target harness's action space, turning harness guidance into training demonstrations. Fine-tuning on the resulting trajectories internalizes harness-induced behavior into the model, so the specialized harness can be removed at deployment. Our experiments spanning knowledge work, tool use, and science domains show that: (1) For frontier LLMs using the same evolved harness, agent-as-harness outperforms code-as-harness. (2) With the specialized harness removed at deployment, Harness-Zero improves the base model's macro-average task success from 23.3% to 44.3%, even exceeding the 41.7% it reaches with that harness still attached. (3) Harness-Zero recovers harness-induced behaviors absent from the base model, with 82.3% average recovery across 28 patterns in the three domains.

范明明老师实验室.title: SFVO: Decoupled Confidence-Guided Stereo-Flow Visual Odometry with Bidirectional PnP
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Kai Zhang, Guoyang Zhao, Jun Ma
范明明老师实验室.summary: SFVO introduces a novel stereo visual odometry framework leveraging pretrained models and decoupled confidence maps to enhance pose estimation accuracy and reliability.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Deep learning-based visual odometry (VO) has achieved significant progress, yet most existing methods focus on a monocular approach, which suffers from scale ambiguity. Stereo VO provides real metric by its nature, but remains less studied in deep learning VO due to its high computational cost and modeling complexity. Recent advances in stereo matching and optical flow estimation have made dense visual correspondence increasingly accurate and reliable, but their complementary geometric information has not been fully exploited for VO. In this paper, we present SFVO, a correspondence-driven stereo VO framework that directly builds upon pretrained stereo matching and optical flow models. SFVO exploits pretrained stereo matching and optical flow models to estimate stereo and temporal correspondences. Instead of learning pose directly from images, SFVO maps learned correspondences into geometric constraints and predicts which points are trustworthy. To improve the reliability of visual correspondence-based geometric constraints, we introduce decoupled confidence maps for rotation and translation. This design better aligns the characteristics of visual correspondence and 6-DoF transformations. Extensive experiments on outdoor and indoor datasets demonstrate that SFVO achieves robust and accurate pose estimation with strong generalization capability. The code will be released.

范明明老师实验室.title: 4DGS-Fixer: Generative Sparse-View 4D Gaussian Splatting with Iterative Refinement Guided by Video Diffusion Priors
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Haitao Huang, Shenghao Zhao, Boyuan Tian, Shin-Fang Chng, Songlin Yang
范明明老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces 4DGS-Fixer, an iterative refinement framework utilizing video diffusion priors to enhance dynamic scene synthesis from sparse-view videos, significantly improving geometric initialization and representation accuracy.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of dynamic scene synthesis from sparse-view videos. Existing methods employ geometric priors, adaptive optimization, or density-control strategies to improve 4D Gaussian modeling under sparse observations. However, they cannot fundamentally resolve the ill-posed problem caused by insufficient observations and missing scene information. Moreover, sparse-view 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) often suffers from poor geometric initialization: with only a few input views, COLMAP typically reconstructs sparse and incomplete point clouds, leaving large scene regions without sufficient Gaussian support and making them difficult to recover through subsequent optimization. To address these limitations, we propose a novel iterative refinement framework based on a video diffusion model to improve the completeness and consistency of dynamic 4D scenes. Specifically, we first estimate multi-view depth maps and fuse them into dense point clouds to provide more complete geometric initialization for a dynamic 4DGS representation. We then employ a pretrained video restoration model to refine sequences rendered along novel camera trajectories at different time steps. The restored sequences serve as pseudo-supervision to regularize and iteratively refine the 4DGS representation. Experiments on a widely used benchmark dataset demonstrate that our method substantially outperforms existing baselines, achieving nearly a 2 dB PSNR improvement over the previous best-performing method.

范明明老师实验室.title: Risk-Aware Occupancy for Safety-Oriented End-to-End Autonomous Driving
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Jiaxing Chen, Hengduo Zou, Yiren Zhao, Bolin Gao
范明明老师实验室.summary: The paper presents a risk-aware occupancy model for autonomous driving that enhances safety by predicting and integrating environmental risks into trajectory planning, achieving significant collision reduction.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Sparse representation formulates the environment perception for the end-to-end driving system as a set of discrete elements like objects and lane lines. This formulation meets safety risks in crowded, occluded scenes dealing with unstructured obstacles, uncertain regions, and intricate interactions. In this paper, we propose a dense representation, risk-aware occupancy, to characterize planning-relevant risks in an explicit and uniform manner. It jointly encodes global scene occupancy, map-derived traffic constraints, and future dynamic agent occupancy into a unified BEV map. The unified BEV map captures the risk evidence for trajectory planning in both spatial and temporal dimensions. We design an E2E network, ROIDrive, to realize risk-aware occupancy. It predicts risk-aware occupancy with an independent branch and injects it into planning queries for safety-oriented trajectory generation. In addition, to quantify the safety problem, we introduce RiskOcc4D-nuScenes built upon nuscenes and occ3d-nuscenes. Our risk-aware occupancy yields relative open-loop collision reductions of 52.9% under the UniAD metric and 35.0% under the ST-P3 metric on nuScenes.

范明明老师实验室.title: Driving on Registers, Reasoning on Risk: Risk-Aware Occupancy for Register-Based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Jiaxing Chen, Hengduo Zou, YuKai Qin, Yiren Zhao, Lidong Yu
范明明老师实验室.summary: RRDrive enhances end-to-end autonomous driving by introducing risk-aware occupancy for improved trajectory prediction and candidate selection, achieving significant performance gains over existing methods.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Multimodal trajectory prediction improves behavioral coverage in end-to-end autonomous driving, but existing methods remain limited by sparse scene representations. Incomplete evidence leads to low-quality candidate generation and unreliable ranking among geometrically similar trajectories. On a register-based baseline, bad and poor candidates constitute 19.74% of the candidate set, while the oracle-best candidate ranks only 33.9th on average. We propose RRDrive, which introduces risk-aware occupancy as a dense, temporally aligned, and trajectory-queryable representation. Its global structure guides high-quality multimodal generation, while candidate-conditioned risk queries support fine-grained selection. We further construct RiskOcc4D-NAVSIM with automatic risk annotations. RRDrive achieves a selected-trajectory PDMS of 0.951, representing a 1.5% relative improvement over the baseline (0.937), and improves the average candidate PDMS by 7.7%. In challenging scenes, it improves candidate PDMS by 30.2% and increases the Spearman correlation among good candidates by 0.41, from 0.26 to 0.67. To move beyond this oracle setting, we further develop an external RiskOcc predictor, a perception module that estimates risk-aware occupancy directly from sensor inputs. The competitive performance validates the representation's feasibility.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: PhyMix: Towards Physically Consistent Single-Image 3D Indoor Scene Generation with Implicit--Explicit Optimization
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Dongli Wu, Jingyu Hu, Ka-Hei Hui, Xiaobao Wei, Chengwen Luo
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: PhyMix introduces a framework that integrates a Physics Evaluator to enhance physical consistency in single-image 3D indoor scene generation, improving reliability for robotics and AI applications.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Existing methods for single-image 3D indoor scene generation often produce visually plausible results that violate real-world physical constraints, limiting their reliability in robotics, embodied AI, and virtual environment design. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Physics Evaluator that assesses four aspects (geometric priors, contact, stability, and deployability) through nine sub-constraints, establishing a benchmark for evaluating physical consistency. Our analysis reveals that even state-of-the-art methods produce scenes with substantial physical inconsistencies despite their visual plausibility. To address these limitations, we propose a framework that incorporates feedback from the Physics Evaluator into both training and inference to improve the physical plausibility of generated scenes. Specifically, PhyMix comprises two components: (i) implicit alignment via Scene-GRPO, a critic-free group-relative preference optimization strategy that uses physical evaluations to guide the generator toward physically plausible layouts, and (ii) explicit refinement via verifier-guided agentic repair, which translates evaluator diagnostics into executable scene-editing skills to correct residual violations at inference time. PhyMix unifies physical evaluation, preference-based alignment, and agentic inference-time correction to improve physical plausibility while retaining the observed scene content. Experiments show improvements in reconstruction quality and physical plausibility, while qualitative examples on stylized and real-world images illustrate the applicability of the framework beyond synthetic inputs.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: RIGen: Beyond Action Following with Reciprocal Interaction in Generative Gameplay
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Mengfei Li, Yi Zhang, Xingtong Ge, Lunjie Zhu, Fangyu Lin
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: RIGen introduces a framework for reciprocal interaction in generative gameplay, enhancing player experience through persistent consequences and contextual audiovisual generation in a first-person shooter prototype.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Generative gameplay requires more than immediate responses to player actions.Actions should have persistent consequences, while the generated world should act according to its own state and rules, shaping the player's situation and subsequent choices. Video generation captures local dynamics, but limited history, partially observed game state, and the need for contextual behavior decisions make such interactions difficult to sustain through audiovisual prediction alone. We introduce \rig (Reciprocally Interactive Generation), a framework for reciprocal interaction in generative gameplay. \rig combines persistent state and configurable rules, contextual interaction reasoning, and action-conditioned audiovisual generation. Together, these components make interaction consequences and actor behavior jointly determine generated content while maintaining consistency between game state and visible outcomes. We construct a Xonotic gameplay dataset to train an audiovisual generator for learning dynamics and interactions. Further post-training enables \rigarena, an interactive generative first-person shooter (FPS) prototype. Experiments demonstrate more reliable combat outcomes and reciprocal interaction between the player and the generated world. Project page: https://murphylmf.github.io/RIGen/.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: GeoPano: Towards Geometrically Accurate 3D Reconstruction from a Single Panorama
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Jing OU, Zidong Cao, Liaoyuan Fan, Zhuoxiao Li, Shuai Zhang
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: GeoPano introduces a novel framework for accurate 3D reconstruction from single panoramas by leveraging panoramic-aware attention and hybrid supervision to enhance geometric consistency and detail.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Panoramic 3D reconstruction enables the holistic recovery of complete 360 $^\circ$ scene geometry, offering significant benefits for robotics and AR/VR applications. However, directly estimating geometry from ERP images is inherently challenged by spherical distortions. To reduce spherical projection distortions, a common strategy is to decompose panoramas into distortion-free perspective views, but independently processing these views often introduces cross-view geometric inconsistencies. To address these challenges, we introduce GeoPano, a feed-forward framework for single-view panoramic 3D reconstruction that recovers a geometrically accurate and consistent point cloud from a single panorama. Our approach is driven by two key innovations: First, we propose a panoramic-aware attention aggregator, featuring a streamlined attention architecture equipped with a novel Pano-Attention mechanism, which explicitly exploits the intrinsic spherical geometry of the panorama to guide cross-view interactions, thereby suppressing geometric inconsistencies. Furthermore, we formulate a hybrid supervision strategy to jointly enforce fine-grained local details in perspective space and global structural coherence in spherical space. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms previous SOTA approaches in reconstruction accuracy, geometric consistency, and visual fidelity.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: DocPilot: Interactive Agent Orchestration and Training for Long Visual Document Understanding
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Zhuowen Liang, Xiaotian Lin, Yuyu Luo, Haixun Wang, Nan Tang
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: DocPilot is an innovative framework that enhances long-document understanding by enabling small language models to effectively orchestrate evidence seeking and cross-modal reasoning through adaptive training.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Multimodal long-document question answering requires models to seek sparse evidence across pages and modalities, understand heterogeneous document content, and reason over the collected evidence. Even advanced vision-language models (VLMs) can overlook sparse evidence and struggle with cross-modal reasoning in a single pass. Existing document agents further introduce multi-step interaction, but some still rely on predefined workflows or coarse-grained actions, limiting the flexibility and granularity of document reasoning. We introduce DocPilot, an agentic document framework that supports expressive orchestration and makes complex document solving learnable by small language models (SLMs). DocPilot orchestrates evidence seeking through page-level navigation and fine-grained evidence localization, and integrates local visual inspection, code-based numerical reasoning, and cross-modal reasoning for multimodal understanding. To transfer these capabilities to small models, we propose curriculum-based agentic training that progresses from single-ability learning to adaptive orchestration through supervision from data-grounded reasoning traces and executable interaction trajectories. Across MMLongBench-Doc, DocBench, FinRAGBench-V, and MADQA, DocPilot achieves strong gains with frontier VLM backbones, while DocPilot-4B delivers competitive performance against substantially larger models, demonstrating strong effectiveness and generalization across diverse long-document reasoning settings. The code is available at https://github.com/HKUSTDial/DocPilot.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Hierarchical Building-Floo-Room Framework for Privacy-Preserving Autonomous Delivery in Large-Scale Buildings
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Xu Xiaoji, Luo Rui, Chen Jinhua, Xiang Changying, Zhang Leihan
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: This paper introduces a hierarchical framework for privacy-preserving autonomous delivery in large buildings, optimizing routing and scheduling across building, floor, and room levels.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Autonomous delivery in large scale buildings requires coordinated planning across multiple spatial levels, including building, floor, and room, while ensuring scheduling efficiency. Existing methods often focus solely on algorithmic development, neglecting integration with physical robotic platforms, and rarely validate performance in real world scenarios. Many approaches also overlook hierarchical building structures and room level privacy constraints, limiting practical applicability. To address these challenges, this paper presents a hierarchical delivery framework based on a Building-Floor-Room abstraction, which decomposes the problem across multiple levels to significantly reduce optimization complexity. We formulate a building aware extension of the capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) that explicitly models inter building and inter floor connectivity, room level access constraints, and privacy sensitive areas, enabling globally feasible and privacy compliant task assignment and routing. Based on this hierarchical model, the framework can evaluate delivery efficiency across different building layouts and optimize depot placement for specific configurations. At the execution level, we introduce a novel hardware design for non interactive, privacy preserving delivery, supported by reachability aware distances and a closed loop mapping, localization, and navigation system, ensuring consistency between planned routes and physical navigation. The proposed framework is validated on a real multi sensor robotic platform, demonstrating reliable multi floor delivery with improved path rationality and overall efficiency.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: RSIgen: Reciprocal Self-Improvement for Agentic Visual Generation
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Yidi Liu, Haozhe Wang, Jie Xiao, Kai Zhu, Xueyang Fu
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: RSIgen is a framework for enhancing agentic visual generation through reciprocal self-improvement, optimizing learning allocation, supervision refresh, and curriculum construction for better task performance.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Agentic visual generation produces experience that can improve the native understanding (agent) and generation roles of a unified multimodal backbone, but task success alone does not determine which role should learn. Generator updates can also make the agent's action supervision stale. We introduce RSIgen, a task-centric reciprocal self-improvement framework linking learning allocation, supervision refresh, and recursive curriculum construction. Dynamic Responsibility Routing (DRR) uses matched interventions on evidence, inputs, and supported actions to select learning recipients and construct compatible training targets. After generator learning, RSIgen re-evaluates the relative utility of tested actions with branch inputs held fixed to refresh agent supervision; the retained roles then construct the next curriculum. Across BAGEL, Qwen-Image, and Wan-Image-7B, RSIgen improves AgentGen-Bench Full Overall9 by 3.2--3.3 points over a three-cycle SearchGen adaptation with action costs. Wan controls support allocation gains at matched role-level training exposure, refresh gains at a matched adaptation budget, and benefits from updated curriculum sources while recipients continue learning. In blind evaluation on 200 real-user requests, pooled tie-adjusted preference scores against the same baseline reach 70.0% for task completion and 64.9% for visual quality.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Yuanjian Xu, Jinyi Han, Jianing Hao, Yuxuan Sun, Fanyang Lu
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: The paper introduces AgentPerturb, a framework for evaluating LLM agent robustness against controlled perturbations, revealing vulnerabilities and guiding robustness-oriented training strategies.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Real-world tasks are often complex and noisy, posing substantial challenges for LLM agents. Yet existing evaluations lack a systematic framework for jointly characterizing potential perturbation targets and types. We use this two-dimensional view to conduct a unified study that quantifies the robustness of current frontier models, traces the mechanisms behind perturbation-induced failures, and draws implications for robustness-oriented training. Through controlled evaluations on APEX-Agents and Toolathlon, we find that perturbations consistently degrade performance, while the dominant vulnerabilities vary across task environments. Trajectory-level analysis reveals that agents rarely recognize altered inputs and often propagate corrupted information without verification. A focused cost analysis further shows that successful perturbed trajectories can require substantially more computation. These findings motivate training objectives that cover diverse forms of noise and reward verification, uncertainty awareness, and recovery. We provide a rigorous benchmark-construction pipeline. Code and data will be released at https://github.com/xuyj233/AgentPerturb.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Anvil: Scaling Embodied Spatial Intelligence through Knowledge Recirculation
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Weilin Ruan, Bohan Zhou, Jinghao Li, Yangkai Wei, Wenqian Li
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: Anvil is a unified framework enhancing embodied spatial intelligence through innovative data generation, training, and benchmarking, significantly outperforming existing models in various benchmarks.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Embodied spatial intelligence requires more than visual recognition: models must localize entities, reason about their relations, and express this knowledge in action-relevant forms. Yet joint training can conflate the knowledge needed at different stages because supervision is fragmented across incompatible geometric and semantic outputs. We introduce Anvil, a unified framework for data generation, training, and benchmarking for embodied spatial intelligence. (1) Anvil-Gen is a heterogeneous data flywheel that combines form-specific generation, cross-stage consistency verification, and failure-driven recollection across 11 Ground--Relation--Act forms. (2) Anvil-Ben provides scene-aligned supervision for learning diverse embodied spatial capabilities and scene-linked assessments that distinguish stage competence from error propagation. (3) Anvil-MOPD is a 9B student that consolidates heterogeneous spatial knowledge through distillation from specialist teachers. Semantic-first-fault routing targets teacher supervision to the student's earliest decisive failure, while stage normalization controls the loss scale across native outputs of different lengths. We construct 5.8M source-grounded records spanning 160K images, reserving 580K spatial records for held-out evaluation and using the remaining 5.22M records for training. On average across seven public benchmarks, Anvil-MOPD outperforms Qwen3.5-9B and RynnBrain-8B by 9.29 and 11.03 percentage points, respectively, while reaching 80.67% on VABench-Point. Controlled studies support targeted coverage, selective transfer, and feedback-guided repair as complementary framework components.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: TS-WAM: Temporal Latent Actions and World-Action Coupling for Vision-Language Robot Control
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Menghao Yin, Jiaju Yin, Xiyue Dong, Lixin Xu, Zhenhui Zhang
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: TS-WAM introduces a self-supervised framework for vision-language robot control that enhances generalization and robustness by predicting future visual states from diverse data sources.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Many vision-language-action policies rely on action-labeled robot demonstrations and lack an explicit mechanism for predicting future visual states. These limitations hinder learning from action-free videos and can encourage overfitting to demonstration conditions, weakening generalization and robustness. We present TS-WAM, a lightweight Teacher-Student World-Action Model that addresses these challenges through self-supervised temporal learning and explicit future prediction. Its vlm-jepa framework learns from heterogeneous data, including robot demonstrations and action-free human videos, using an EMA target branch without requiring a separately trained external teacher. By coupling vlm-jepa with delta-lwm, TS-WAM learns to predict latent actions from the current observation and instruction and uses them to predict future visual features that guide action generation at inference. A unified end-to-end training architecture jointly optimizes temporal representation learning, visual dynamics, and robot control without a separate latent-action or world-model pretraining stage. The EMA target branch is removed at inference, keeping the deployed policy lightweight. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and SimplerEnv, together with real-world manipulation experiments on Franka Research 3 and RevoTron, demonstrate that TS-WAM achieves strong manipulation performance, generalization, and robustness.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Grounding Generative Verification in 3D Content
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Shuanglin Li, Jiaying Lin, Shuquan Ye
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: The paper presents 3DVerifierBench, a benchmark for evaluating verification in 3D generation, highlighting the need for reliable feedback to improve task-specific correctness and system refinement.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and 3D generation have expanded 3D understanding and synthesis. However, beyond visual fidelity, task-specific correctness grounded in 3D evidence remains a major challenge. We argue that building reliable 3D systems requires not only stronger generation and reasoning, but also verification feedback that identifies unmet requirements and explains their violations, allowing systems to reflect on and refine their outputs. Such feedback must integrate multi-view observations and distinguish genuine inconsistencies from projection-dependent appearances. We make three contributions. First, we introduce 3DVerifierBench, a benchmark spanning 10 tasks that evaluates decisions, rejection explanations, and responses to controlled changes in specifications and candidates. A human study reveals a 21.6 percentage-point gap between humans and the strongest tested model, GPT-6 Astra, while explanation-aware analysis exposes weaknesses in rejection reliability. Second, we analyze verification across fine-grained factual categories, exposing errors in values and target binding. We develop a scalable pipeline combining multi-view fact extraction, controlled 3D editing, and native annotations to produce 14,126 training examples with contradiction explanations and linked counterfactuals. Third, we examine how verification could support 3D generation through candidate selection and recursive refinement. In human-labeled sixteen-candidate pools, oracle selection improves complete factual success from 26.7% to 90.0%. In a separate eight-input study, human-guided recursive refinement satisfies all seven requirements for every input, compared with three under parallel Oracle@8. Together, our benchmark, analysis, and data pipeline establish a foundation for models to reflect on 3D content through reliable verification feedback.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Blame Errant Words, Not the Canvas: Defect-Aware Spatial Credit Assignment for Visual Text Generation
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Sujie Hu, Huaisong Zhang, Pujing Yang, Qian Wang, Xiaomin Li
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: The paper presents TextDART and SCANNER, a defect-aware approach for visual text generation that enhances feedback precision, improving text accuracy and glyph fidelity.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Recent reinforcement learning approaches have improved visual text generation, yet generated images still suffer from incorrect wording and malformed glyphs. We identify two coupled limitations: recognition-based rewards often overlook visible glyph defects, while whole-image scalar feedback obscures the uneven quality of individual text regions. These limitations motivate our central principle: $\textit{Blame errant words, not the canvas}$, to effectively preserve local quality distinctions. First, we introduce $\mathbf{TextDART}$, a defect-aware region-targeted reward model that localizes individual text regions and independently evaluates their semantic correctness and glyph quality, providing fine-grained, region-precise feedback. Building on TextDART, we propose $\mathbf{SCANNER}$, which turns these regional judgments into spatially differentiated policy feedback. It normalizes rewards for each text target across sampled images and casts the resulting regional advantages onto the corresponding latent tokens. Extensive experiments on existing benchmarks and our newly established $\textbf{PolyText-Bench}$ demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in text accuracy and glyph fidelity. Project page: https://sujiehu.github.io/textdart-scanner

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: This paper reviews and analyzes the integration of reinforcement learning into diffusion models, addressing limitations and proposing strategies for improved goal-directed generation across various applications.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Chuyue Li, Jinpeng Yu, Haozhe Wang, Tian Xueyun, Zhijing Zhang
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: The AVA-Encoder transforms finished films into agent-native representations via a Film Knowledge Graph, enhancing video creation quality and enabling improved editing and downstream applications.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Agentic video creation systems remain far from cinematic-grade quality: their underlying models struggle to plan how story, characters, visuals, and sound fit together, and high-quality creation trajectories to learn such planning abilities are scarce. Finished human films embody this knowledge, but in a tightly coupled audiovisual form that agents cannot directly read or manipulate. We propose the Agentic Video Auto-Encoder (AVA-Encoder), which works backward from finished films, turning them into agent-native representations with reconstruction itself as supervision. It encodes a film into a Film Knowledge Graph (Film KG) of structured-text nodes, typed dependency edges, and linked multimodal assets, then regenerates the film from this graph with a fixed decoder. Reconstruction residuals are distilled into textual gradients that drive dual-loop self-evolution: an outer loop learns a shared encoding policy across videos, and an inner loop refines each video's Film KG at test time. AVA-Encoder improves reconstruction fidelity by 20.7 percentage points over the strongest baseline; its learned policy outperforms a finely human-tuned policy with over 70 percent fewer system-prompt tokens; and Film KGs support coordinated editing and improve all tested downstream creation systems. We release the framework, a reconstruction benchmark, and a Film KG dataset.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: ReEnvision: Future-Guided Selective Action Repair for Long-Horizon Manipulation
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Xiyin Zeng, Xuewei Huang, Yi Lu, Weihao Yuan, Hao Wang
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: ReEnvision introduces a future-guided selective action repair framework for long-horizon robotic manipulation, enhancing action success rates by preserving valid actions amid execution deviations.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires robust execution over sequences of interdependent actions. Existing methods typically handle execution deviations by replanning the remaining action chunk or correcting actions step by step as new observations arrive. However, a local deviation may affect only a few actions under distribution shift, yet replanning regenerates the entire chunk from an unfamiliar state, potentially introducing errors into otherwise valid actions. Step-wise correction may react too late, as it does not explicitly anticipate how the deviation affects subsequent actions. We propose ReEnvision, a future-guided selective action repair framework that updates a joint future-action belief using execution feedback. It then learns how the resulting belief revision affects each unexecuted action. The resulting belief revision enables selective repair of only the affected actions within a cached action chunk, preserving valid actions and reserving full replanning for severe deviations. On CALVIN, L-CALVIN, and RLBench, ReEnvision achieves 86.6% 5-step success, improves 10-step success from 56% to 63%, and reaches an average success rate of 88.8%, respectively. On five real-world manipulation tasks, it achieves an average success rate of 82.8%. Controlled repair experiments further demonstrate the benefits of localizing affected actions and preserving valid ones during execution.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Synergistic Vision-Language Reinforcement Enables Scalable On-Demand Analysis across Diverse Clinical Tasks
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Haonan Wang, Jiaji Mao, Lehan Wang, Qixiang Zhang, Marawan Elbatel
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: SyRe is a vision-language reinforcement model that enhances tumor and organ segmentation in oncology through diverse prompts and extensive training data, achieving high accuracy and generalization.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Accurate segmentation of tumors and organs-at-risk is essential for oncology but remains time-consuming and expertise-intensive. Existing AI systems often require manual spatial prompts or task-specific retraining, while generic class labels provide limited guidance for heterogeneous disease targets. Here we present SyRe, a text-prompted segmentation foundation model based on Synergistic vision-language Reinforcement, which strengthens bidirectional interaction between visual and linguistic representations. We introduce Color Region Description (CRD) to generate region-level semantic supervision and construct SyReData, comprising 20 million image-mask-description triplets across 9 modalities and 229 segmentation tasks. Training with diversified prompt formats enables single-target, multi-target and open-ended segmentation, together with invalid-prompt rejection. SyRe achieves accurate segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios, with strong gains on disease-related targets. Evaluation on 28 unseen external datasets, including 17 cancer types, 3 non-cancer diseases and multinational in-house cohorts, demonstrates generalization under distribution shift. Beyond spatial overlap, SyRe-generated masks preserve quantitative pathology information. Across five retrospective tumor imaging cohorts spanning CT and MRI, radiomics derived from these masks stratify survival and improve prognostic modeling over clinical baselines. Clinician-in-the-loop refinement further supports case-level correction. These results establish SyRe as a generalizable framework for scalable quantitative oncology analysis and clinician-guided segmentation.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Interlock: From Local Correctness to Task Completion in Long-Horizon Agents
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Linji Hao, Yanji He, Zihan Wang, Hansi Yang, Jiayuan Zhang
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: The Interlock framework enhances long-horizon task completion in agents by using a typed completion graph to maintain relationships among tasks, improving performance metrics across various benchmarks.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Large language model agents increasingly undertake long-horizon tasks in complex environments characterized by fragmented evidence, partially completed states, and dependencies across resources and artifacts. Existing agents may satisfy individual requirements while failing to maintain these relationships, producing locally correct but incomplete outcomes. These failures arise because task completion depends on relationships among environmental evidence, consequential decisions, and required effects. To address this completion gap, we propose Interlock, a framework for task synthesis that represents each task as a typed completion graph. Grounding edges connect public evidence to decisions, coupling hyperedges impose joint constraints across components, and realization edges connect decisions to all required downstream effects. Interlock compiles this graph into a resettable workspace, a public request, and an evaluation rubric. A source-coverage review checks whether the original requirements survive generation, while a public-input review checks whether the rubric is supported by the materials available to the solver. An agent-as-judge inspects execution artifacts and runs verification scripts, retaining trajectories judged to satisfy all mandatory requirements. To evaluate training utility, we fine-tune two Qwen3.6 backbones on their own accepted trajectories. Across the two backbones, training improves AutomationBench task pass rates by 4.00-4.50 percentage points, JobBench weighted scores by 3.20-6.64 points, and Harvey LAB criterion pass rates by 3.89-4.16 percentage points. These results demonstrate the training utility of the synthesized experience across external task environments.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Refine Actions If Needed: Adaptive Action Chunk Refinement for Robot Manipulation
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Hanlin Liu, Zichen Zhou, Jiacheng Zhang, Liuyuan Na, Jin Jin
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: RAIN is a framework that adaptively refines robot manipulation actions by predicting error levels, enhancing task success while minimizing inference latency.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Computationally lightweight manipulation policies predict executable actions with low inference latency, but prediction errors can limit task success. Iterative generative policies can achieve higher task success rates, but repeated network evaluations increase inference latency. Refining action proposals from computationally lightweight policies can combine these strengths, but the amount of refinement needed varies across states. We introduce RAIN (Refine Actions If Needed), a framework that predicts action errors at different refinement levels to decide whether and how much to refine each executable proposal, before performing any refinement. We train an ensemble to predict these errors by comparing action proposals and their refined versions with expert actions from offline demonstrations, without requiring explicit labels of refinement needs. Calibration balances uncertainty, computation, and temporal consistency. We evaluate RAIN on eight ManiSkill tasks and four real-robot tasks. In simulation, our policy achieves 66.6% success, approaching the best evaluated diffusion-policy success rate with 5.71 times lower policy latency. On the real robot, success increases from 55.0% with Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) to 72.5%, with comparable average successful completion time. Matched controls show that dynamic routing maintains the strongest observed fixed-refinement success level with 26.6% fewer refiner evaluations. Project page: https://rain-policy.github.io/.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: GeoCloak: An Agentic Framework for Semantics-Preserving Geolocation Privacy via Peripheral Clue Manipulation
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Yixin Wu, Mingjie Li, Yun Shen, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: GeoCloak is a framework that enhances geolocation privacy by manipulating peripheral clues in images while preserving semantic content, significantly reducing location inference accuracy.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: The rapid advancement of large vision language models (LVLMs) has made geolocation inference from images highly accurate and accessible. This poses serious privacy risks: a passive adversary with black-box LVLM access can infer a user's location from a single photo with no metadata. Existing protection methods rely almost exclusively on adversarial perturbation, which introduces perceptible visual artifacts and utility degradation. We identify the visual-geolocation asymmetry: geolocation-decisive clues, such as street signs, tend to be visually peripheral but dominate location inference. Exploiting this asymmetry, we propose GeoCloak, an agentic framework for semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection. It acts as a clue-aware planner that analyzes each image to identify geolocation-relevant clues, dispatches targeted semantic edits to directly suppress peripheral clues, and autonomously configures adversarial perturbation to further suppress residual geolocation features, all under iterative utility-aware feedback. We evaluate GeoCloak on four diverse datasets spanning 108 countries and 576 cities against five LVLMs and three inference methods. GeoCloak reduces overall city-level accuracy from 41.2% to 9.9%, approximately half of the best-performing baseline, while achieving substantially superior utility preservation both qualitatively and quantitatively. We hope this work takes a meaningful step toward practical, semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection, giving users greater control over the location information inadvertently embedded in their shared images.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: SkillCommit: Evolving Agent Skills through Behaviorally Validated Scope Expansion
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Yu He, Weikai Yang
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: SkillCommit is an online framework that evolves agent skills by preserving instance-specific experiences and hierarchically abstracting behaviorally validated strategies to enhance performance.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can continually improve without parameter updates by converting historical experience into reusable procedural knowledge. However, existing methods often consolidate experience based on semantic similarity or LLM judgments, which may merge superficially related but behaviorally incompatible strategies and thereby degrade performance. To address the issue, we propose SkillCommit, an online skill evolution framework that continuously transforms experience into a hierarchical library of reusable skills. Rather than generalizing from individual experiences immediately, SkillCommit first preserves each experience as an instance-specific patch, retaining its locally validated behavior. As patches accumulate, SkillCommit abstracts those sharing a common behavioral mechanism into higher-level skills. Specifically, for each incoming skill, embedding-based retrieval first identifies candidate related skills. Cross-instance replay and an LLM-based mechanism check determine whether these skills transfer across cases and share a common underlying mechanism. Candidates that pass both checks are abstracted into a higher-level skill and committed only if it preserves the validated behavior of all constituent skills. Experiments on RuleArena, OpenExempt and KOR-Bench demonstrate that SkillCommit consistently improves agent performance across diverse domains. Moreover, the learned skills transfer across model scales and families, enabling cross-model experience transfer.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Wei Chen, Yubing Wu, Zhou Xu, Haoyue Zhang, Delu Zeng
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR) improves token credit assignment in RLVR by using single-rollout updates based on future outcomes, outperforming GRPO in efficiency and maintaining accuracy.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains language models from checked task outcomes, but assigning a terminal reward to individual reasoning tokens or actions remains difficult. Group-relative methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) sample several attempts per prompt, but lose their reward-based learning signal when all attempts receive the same outcome. We propose Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR), a single-rollout method that turns a completed trajectory's own future into token-level update weights. The generating policy snapshot scores each eligible token under its causal history and under a hindsight context containing the realized future and verifier feedback. A normalized Jensen--Shannon divergence between the two views weights the reward relative to a historical baseline, yielding bounded token credit for both successful and failed attempts, with no reference solution or learned critic. In paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared $100$-step schedule, HP-RLVR trains $1.21\times$, $1.46\times$, and $2.30\times$ faster than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld, using one eighth the rollouts per prompt. Accuracy is comparable overall, with HP-RLVR ahead on mathematics at all three sizes and GRPO ahead on code and ALFWorld. In ALFWorld, $43.2\%$ (4B) and $49.0\%$ (8B) of GRPO's gradient-norm records are zero, versus none for HP-RLVR.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: EvoSpatial: Experience-Driven Skill and Tool Evolution for Spatial Reasoning Agents
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Bin Yu, Shijie Lian, Zhaolong Shen, Xiaopeng Lin, Yao Zhang
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: EvoSpatial is a framework that enhances spatial reasoning agents by evolving skills and tools through execution feedback, improving performance across multiple benchmarks without requiring ground-truth data.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Spatial reasoning agents can inspect tool outputs and repair errors, but reusing these lessons requires preserving both the computation and the conditions that make it valid. We introduce EvoSpatial, a framework that learns from execution experience by updating a library of linked skills and tools. Skills describe procedures, geometric assumptions, and verification steps; tools implement the operations those procedures require. When solving a task, the agent retrieves relevant skills and synthesizes reusable computational functions if existing tools are insufficient. After each task, execution feedback and evidence checks guide skill revision and tool consolidation, without ground-truth answers or benchmark scores. Across 20 benchmarks, EvoSpatial averages 63.9, 4.0 percentage points above the average reported by SpatialClaw. The evolved library also improves held-out and cross-benchmark performance when updates are disabled, and trajectories generated with evolved skills improve supervised fine-tuning, even without external skills at evaluation. Keeping checked procedures on record, together with the tools that support them, lets an agent carry spatial reasoning experience from one task to the next.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Why Do VLMs Fail at Remote Physiological Measurement? Rethinking with Physiological Grounding and Numerical Alignment
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).authors_text: Xiao Yang, Zekun Zhang, Yuxuan Fan, Duoxun Tang, Ziyang Liu
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).summary: The paper introduces VITAL, a framework enhancing Vision-Language Models for remote physiological measurement by aligning visual and physiological data while improving numerical accuracy.
机器人研究所 (CKSRI).debug_abstract: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. However, existing RPM methods rely on task-specific models and cannot be seamlessly integrated with the multimodal understanding and interaction capabilities of VLMs. We revisit RPM with VLMs and provide empirical evidence for two major bottlenecks: generic visual semantic representations fail to preserve fine-grained physiological cues; while discrete token prediction in autoregressive generation is inherently misaligned with continuous numerical measurement. To address these challenges, we propose VITAL (Visual-physiological Token Alignment for Language Models), a visual-physiological token alignment framework for RPM and preserving general vision tasks. VITAL retains the original visual pathway for semantic understanding and introduces an independent physiological pathway to jointly model semantic and physiological information. Moreover, we propose a structured numerical alignment approach to improve the reliability of generative heart rate estimation by enhancing numerical relationship modeling. Extensive experiments show that VITAL improves cross-domain estimation performance on multiple rPPG datasets while preserving the general visual understanding capability of VLMs, demonstrating its effectiveness as a unified visual-physiological model. Code will be released.

机器人研究所 (CKSRI).title: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence
