Across 315 fixed-output simulation windows, 45.21% of response-top20 positions fall outside error-top20, revealing information beyond prediction error. Videos and further details are available on the project website: https://rapwam.github.io/.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Ningxin Pan, Hanyu Li, Yeqing Shen, Ning Ding, Yehui Tang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents RealtimeBench for evaluating LLM agents in dynamic environments and introduces TORSI, enhancing agent performance through structured learning and real-time adaptation.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. Two rounds raise Jev's average test score from 13.51 to 24.19 on a 0--100 progress scale, improving all six game types. The instructions also improve average scores for three other models without retuning. These findings point toward real-time intelligence: enabling powerful LLM agents to remain effective in a continuously changing world by organizing deliberation, learning, and action across timescales.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: ReasonUni: Reasoning-Augmented Reconstruction Advances Unified Multimodal Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Feize Wu, Zhiyuan Yan, Yuhuan Hong, Yuwei Niu, Zongjian Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: ReasonUni enhances unified multimodal models by integrating reasoning into reconstructive post-training, improving image-to-text understanding and text-to-image generation through a novel reinforcement learning approach.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Image-to-text (I2T) understanding and text-to-image (T2I) generation are dual tasks in unified multimodal models (UMMs). Reconstructive post-training couples these tasks, but existing reconstruction-based methods remain perception-centric and provide limited supervision for reasoning about structure, intent, and transformation. We propose ReasonUni, a reasoning-augmented reconstructive post-training framework that extends this coupling beyond perception. Given an original image and an editing instruction, the UMM first reasons about what and how to edit and describes the target state, then generates the corresponding target image conditioned on this understanding output. To jointly optimize both modules, we introduce TreeGRPO, a tree-structured reinforcement learning method that samples multiple reasoning paths and candidate images per path, then aggregates visual rewards to update both modules under a unified objective. Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate consistent gains in both understanding and generation, showing that reasoning-augmented reconstruction yields genuine mutual gains for UMMs.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Rubric Judgments Lack Uncertainty: Conformal Weighting for LLM Evaluation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Licheng Pan, Haocheng Yang, Haoxuan Li, Yuzhou Chen, Yichen Sun
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces Uncertainty-aware Rubric Weighting (URW), enhancing LLM evaluation by addressing judgment uncertainty through conformal calibration for improved reinforcement learning alignment.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Rubric-based evaluation is widely used to assess large language model (LLM) outputs by decomposing quality into multiple criteria and assigning each a binary judgment from an LLM verifier. However, judgment certainty varies substantially across criteria. Existing methods uniformly aggregate these judgments into a final score, implicitly treating every criterion as equally certain and overlooking this heterogeneity. As a result, uncertain judgments remain incorporated into reward estimation without distinction, potentially yielding misleading training signals for downstream reinforcement learning (RL). To address this limitation, we propose Uncertainty-aware Rubric Weighting (URW), a training-free framework that quantifies criterion-level judgment uncertainty via conformal calibration. Specifically, URW elicits a soft uncertainty signal from a fixed pool of paraphrased judgment templates and converts it into a per-criterion weight using split-conformal $p$-values with provable coverage guarantees. Extensive experiments demonstrate that URW consistently improves pairwise preference accuracy and delivers stronger downstream RL alignment.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Mallea: Building, Steering, and Memorizing Worlds with Coding Agent
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xuanyi Liu, Ruiqi Li, Siwei Ma
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Mallea is a coding agent system that builds, steers, and memorizes dynamic worlds from text by coordinating object representations, rules, and visual memory.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Code world models represent world dynamics through explicit state and executable rules. We investigate how to coordinate object representations, behavioral revisions, and visual memory within this formulation. We present Mallea, a system for building, steering, and memorizing worlds from text. A coding agent infers object interaction requirements from the prompt and jointly plans object structure, properties, and rules, favoring compact representations that support those requirements. The world evolves under the planned rules; optional user actions steer it, while text requests can edit properties or extend capabilities with unaffected state preserved. Object texture memory retains reusable appearance only for whitebox-defined objects and adapts it as those objects change. The program advances world state, while a generative renderer combines current structure with remembered appearance. By organizing construction, intervention, and memory around the same objects, Mallea conditions subsequent observations on the latest state and compatible appearance. Project page: https://lxycopper.github.io/Mallea.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: CQDC-Warp: GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Quasi-Dynamic Simulation for Contact-Rich Manipulation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yanchen Ding, Jiayi Chen, Jianfeng Xu, Wei Zhao, Li Yi
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: CQDC-Warp is a GPU-accelerated differentiable simulator that enhances contact-rich trajectory optimization for robots, achieving higher success rates and significantly faster planning times.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Efficient synthesis of contact-rich manipulation trajectories is essential for downstream robot learning. Gradient-based planning offers a promising approach, but jointly optimizing motion and contact decisions remains challenging. Meanwhile, many existing planners run on CPUs with limited throughput. We present CQDC-Warp, a GPU-accelerated differentiable quasi-dynamic simulator for batched model predictive control (MPC). We use it to study contact-guided trajectory optimization, in which intended robot--object contacts are specified before planning and encouraged through soft costs, while the simulated dynamics determine contact geometry and frictional response without a prescribed contact-mode schedule. Across $17{,}408$ trials on the $17$-object Allegro in-hand rotation benchmark, our framework achieves $79.8\%$ success, compared with $73.7\%$ for CFree and $65.2\%$ for IMPACT, and reduces mean trajectory-generation time by factors of $27.0$ and $50.2$, respectively. On a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 with $2{,}048$ parallel worlds, forward and backward throughput reach $2.06\times10^5$ and $2.25\times10^5$ world-steps per second, respectively. Further experiments cover manipulation with LEAP and Shadow hands, environmental contact exploitation, bimanual manipulation, whole-body control, and real-world trajectory replay on a Sharpa hand.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: From Agent Traces to Trust: A Survey of Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yiqi Wang, Jiaqi Zhang, Zhangkai Wu, Taotao Cai, Zirui Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This survey presents a unified framework for analyzing execution provenance and evidence tracing in LLM agents, highlighting gaps in current research and proposing future directions.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are moving beyond text generation to planning, tool use, retrieval, memory access, environmental interaction, and multi-agent collaboration. Because their outputs depend on information and execution steps across an agent run, their execution processes are difficult to verify, debug, and audit. Even a correct final answer does not reveal which evidence supported its claims, whether tool calls were justified, how memory shaped decisions, or where execution failures originated. Relevant research addresses these questions across evidence attribution, tool-use safety, agent memory, and observability, but these areas emphasize different parts of the execution process. This survey brings them into a common framework through execution provenance, a typed graph of an agent run, and evidence tracing, its projection onto evidence-support relations, distinguishing evidence that supports a conclusion from execution that influences it. We introduce a six-dimensional taxonomy covering trace sources, evidence and execution units, provenance relations, tracing granularity and timing, representation forms, and trust functions, complemented by operational definitions of nine provenance relations and two cross-cutting attributes, provenance origin and trace assurance. Applying this framework to the surveyed systems and benchmarks reveals three gaps: limited integration of fine-grained provenance with multiple trust functions, no benchmark in our catalog that evaluates the complete provenance chain, and little reporting of tamper-evident or attested traces. These findings motivate research on unified trace schemas, semantic provenance, memory and multi-agent lineage, provenance-aware safety and recovery, realistic benchmarks, trace assurance, and privacy-aware auditing. Resources are available at https://github.com/xiaoqi-7/Agent-Tracing-Survey.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: TOPS: First-Principles Visual Token Pruning via Constructing Token Optimal Preservation Sets for Efficient MLLM Inference
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Tinghao Wang, Yichen Guo, Rui Huang, Junchi Yao, Qizhe Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents TOPS, a novel visual token pruning method for multimodal large language models that optimally preserves task-relevant tokens while enhancing efficiency and performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved strong multimodal reasoning capabilities, but their efficiency is limited by the large number of visual tokens, which introduces substantial computational overhead. Visual token pruning offers a natural solution, yet existing methods are imperfect: attention-based criteria tend to retain redundant tokens, while diversity-based criteria are often agnostic to user instructions. Even methods that combine multiple criteria still lack a principled formulation of the intrinsic objective of token pruning. In this paper, we revisit visual token pruning from a first-principles perspective and formulate it as constructing Token Optimal Preservation Sets. Through a top-down information-theoretic analysis, we identify three fundamental principles for effective token selection: Task Relevance, Information Coverage, and Semantic Diversity. Based on these principles, we propose TOPS, a training-free and model-agnostic pruning module that can be applied to various MLLMs. Extensive experiments on 7 MLLM backbones and 14 benchmarks demonstrate that TOPS outperforms prior methods under diverse pruning settings. Notably, on LLaVA-NeXT, TOPS removes 77.8% of visual tokens while preserving 100.0% and 100.6% performance on its 7B and 13B models, respectively, suggesting that pruning redundant visual tokens can sometimes mitigate hallucination and inspire future lightweight MLLM design. Our code is available at https://github.com/MAX-7237/TOPS.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Router Drift Control: Mitigating Off-Policy Degradation in Mixture-of-Experts Reinforcement Learning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Liangyao Jin, Zhixin Wang, Liming Liu, Mingjun Zhang, Zhengzhou Zhu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Router Drift Control (RDC) mitigates off-policy degradation in Mixture-of-Experts reinforcement learning by filtering high-drift responses, enhancing accuracy during asynchronous training.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can become off-policy due to training-inference mismatch, mini-batch updates, and asynchronous training.The resulting mismatch is especially harmful in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where rollout--training discrepancies can change routing decisions and lead to router drift. Rollout Routing Replay (R3) mitigates this mismatch by reusing expert selections from the rollout stage during training. Our analysis shows that routing replay introduces gradient bias by losing contributions from experts selected by the training router but not the rollout router. To address this, we propose Router Drift Control (RDC), which uses routing disagreement between rollout and training as a signal of off-policy staleness and selectively rejects high-drift responses. The sequence-level filtering avoids gradient bias introduced by replay while preserving native expert selection and the associated learning signals for retained responses. Experiments show that RDC achieves larger gains as policy staleness increases and remains effective in asynchronous RL. In asynchronous training, RDC combined with Truncated Importance Sampling (TIS) improves the average peak validation accuracy across AIME 2024 and AIME 2025 by 5.5 points over TIS and 4.5 points over R3.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Uni-PNP: Unified Prehensile and Non-prehensile Policy Learning for Generalizable Object Pose Reaching
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Wenxuan Zhu, Yuze Wang, Jiangran Lyu, Jiayi Chen, Yixin Zheng
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Uni-PNP introduces a unified policy for joint learning of prehensile and non-prehensile manipulation, achieving significant success in diverse object pose reaching tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Object manipulation often requires combining non-prehensile actions with grasping. However, existing approaches typically develop these capabilities separately and integrate them by sequencing distinct primitives through prescribed intermediate objectives, limiting the coordination of contact motions and grasping. Their integration also remains sensitive to object and gripper geometry and depends on particular environmental supports, complicating real-world deployment. We present Uni-PNP, a unified policy that jointly learns prehensile and non-prehensile manipulation for object pose reaching across diverse objects and grippers. To achieve this, we first pretrain a geometry encoder to predict contact-induced object motion using a contact-dynamics dataset constructed from simulated interactions between diverse objects and grippers. We then train the policy in a two-stage reinforcement learning curriculum from graspable objects to ungraspable peers, encouraging the discovery of non-prehensile interactions and their integration with grasping. Experiments show 76.39% success on hundreds of seen objects with grippers, and 57.91% on unseen peers, outperforming the strongest pose-reaching baseline by 20.52 and 17.79 percentage points, respectively. We also analyze emergent behaviors, including nonprehensile and prehensile repositioning, grasp acquisition that requires grasping after tipping, and table-assisted reorientation while grasping, and transfer to the real-world scenario. Project page available at lgswdn.github.io/Uni-PNP.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: What Should Robot Policies Learn to Predict? Rethinking Supervision Targets in Vision-Language-Action Learning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Haitao Shen, Hanyu Liu, Yihan Lin, Huiping Liu, Junbo Cui
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper proposes a unified framework for vision-language-action learning that optimally allocates training samples between action prediction and auxiliary objectives, enhancing policy performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are typically trained with action prediction as the primary supervision signal, since robots ultimately execute actions. Auxiliary objectives such as latent-action (LA) and future-vision (FV) prediction are often added to improve policy learning, yet they compete with action prediction for the same training budget. We ask whether, under a fixed budget, allocating a substantial share of training samples to such objectives, rather than to further action prediction, can improve policy learning. We build a unified VLA framework that couples a two-stream multimodal diffusion transformer (MMDiT) with a sample-level router, which assigns each training sample to either action prediction or an auxiliary objective and thus makes supervision allocation explicit. Within this framework, we instantiate three LA targets based on LAPA and its DINO-feature variants, and three FV targets based on DINOv3, V-JEPA 2, and Wan2.2 representations. Across LIBERO, CALVIN, and four real-robot tasks, suitable LA and FV supervision outperforms action-only training under the same budget, even when action prediction receives no more than half of the training samples. FV generally outperforms LA, although the strongest LA target remains competitive on CALVIN. Diagnostic analyses suggest that DINO-based LA targets emphasize relative motion, whereas FV targets emphasize absolute position and task identity. We therefore argue that what robot policies learn to predict, and how training is allocated among these targets, should be treated as explicit design choices rather than defaulting to action-dominant training.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: When Reasoning Is Not Enough: Proactive Inquiry for Cross-Modal Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Wei Cai, Jian Zhao, Yuchen Yuan, Xuelong Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces SAFE-PRO, a proactive inquiry method that enhances safety in multimodal large language models by addressing intent-level risks through a risk-conditioned uncertainty signal.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can act unsafely when individually benign images and texts are interpreted jointly. Beyond implicit reasoning risk, where reasoning drifts toward harm, we identify intent-level risk, where cross-modal ambiguity silently commits the model to a hazardous premise that path-level optimization alone cannot correct. We propose SAFE-PRO, which uses a Risk-Conditioned Uncertainty (RCU) signal, combining predictive entropy with a learned cross-modal risk score, to decide when to ask safety-grounded clarifying questions and where to apply path optimization, under a reward that prioritizes safety and penalizes over-refusal. We also build SSUI-Dialog, a multimodal multi-turn dataset with dual-intent supervision, and theoretically analyze gradient variance and unsafe-completion risk under RCU. Across seven benchmarks and two base MLLMs, SAFE-PRO consistently improves safety over SRPO, roughly halves its over-refusal, and surpasses GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet in average single-turn safety.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Memory as Weights: Internalizing Long-Term History for Streaming Videos
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zhuoming Liu, Jinhong Lin, Lin Zhang, Yiwu Zhong, Yin Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: MaLoW is a novel streaming memory framework that internalizes historical context as lightweight parameter updates, enhancing video understanding and action success rates in vision-language models.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Streaming vision-language models (VLMs) must continuously integrate information from the past while remaining responsive to current observations and user queries. Existing memory mechanisms typically compress, retrieve, or cache historical observations and reintroduce them into the input context, forcing historical memory and current observations to compete for limited context. We propose MaLoW, a streaming memory framework that instead internalizes historical context into evolving lightweight parameter updates. MaLoW uses a recurrent HyperNetwork to incrementally consolidate incoming video observations into fixed-size LoRA weights, allowing historical information to be carried forward without revisiting the full video stream. In doing so, MaLoW represents history as weights, while keeping the current observation as input. To support training, we further construct MaLoW-Instruct, a large-scale streaming video dataset containing 381K question-answer pairs over 56K videos. We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate that MaLoW achieves strong performance on OVO-Bench, StreamingBench, and StreamArena. On the backward split of OVO-Bench, MaLoW outperforms prior memory approaches by 3.9% to 11.8% across different video backbones while incurring only modest latency overhead. Beyond streaming video understanding, MaLoW also generalizes to vision-language-action models, improving the action success rate on Simpler WidowX by 9.3%.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Huanyao Zhang, Jiepeng Zhou, Jiaye Lin, Ontai Tang, Jingtian Hao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: MMSearch-OPD enhances long-horizon multimodal search agents through targeted data refinement, joint reinforcement learning, and on-policy distillation, improving training and performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Multimodal deep search is moving from short queries to long-horizon investigations that continually acquire evidence. However, training such agents remains constrained by limited challenging training questions and insufficient process feedback. We introduce MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline performs targeted expansion of reasoning chains derived from existing simple multimodal questions. Parameterized transformations control search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements while reusing existing image--question pairs. For training, answer rewards and lightweight behavior penalties guide RL, while the reward gap modulates token-level teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories. An exponentially decaying distillation coefficient reduces teacher dependence as training proceeds. Experiments show gains from data refinement and further improvements from joint training after SFT, indicating stronger long-horizon multimodal deep search capabilities.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: SceneReVis: A Self-Reflective Vision-Grounded Framework for 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis via Multi-Turn RL
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yang Zhao, Shizhao Sun, Meisheng Zhang, Yingdong Shi, Xubo Yang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: SceneReVis introduces a self-reflective framework for 3D indoor scene synthesis that utilizes multi-turn reinforcement learning to resolve spatial conflicts and enhance generation fidelity.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Current one-pass 3D scene synthesis methods often suffer from spatial hallucinations, such as collisions, due to a lack of deliberative reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce SceneReVis, a vision-grounded self-reflection framework that employs an iterative "diagnose-and-act" loop to explicitly intercept and resolve spatial conflicts using multi-modal feedback. To support this step-wise paradigm, we construct SceneChain-12k, a large-scale dataset of causal construction trajectories derived through a novel reverse engineering pipeline. We further propose a two-stage training recipe that transitions from Supervised Fine-Tuning to Agentic Reinforcement Learning, evolving the model into an active spatial planner. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SceneReVis achieves state-of-the-art performance in high-fidelity generation and goal-oriented optimization, with improved transfer to underrepresented room categories in the dataset and promising potential for extension to out-of-distribution room types.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Blame Errant Words, Not the Canvas: Defect-Aware Spatial Credit Assignment for Visual Text Generation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Sujie Hu, Huaisong Zhang, Pujing Yang, Qian Wang, Xiaomin Li
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper presents TextDART and SCANNER, a defect-aware approach for visual text generation that enhances feedback precision, improving text accuracy and glyph fidelity.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Recent reinforcement learning approaches have improved visual text generation, yet generated images still suffer from incorrect wording and malformed glyphs. We identify two coupled limitations: recognition-based rewards often overlook visible glyph defects, while whole-image scalar feedback obscures the uneven quality of individual text regions. These limitations motivate our central principle: $\textit{Blame errant words, not the canvas}$, to effectively preserve local quality distinctions. First, we introduce $\mathbf{TextDART}$, a defect-aware region-targeted reward model that localizes individual text regions and independently evaluates their semantic correctness and glyph quality, providing fine-grained, region-precise feedback. Building on TextDART, we propose $\mathbf{SCANNER}$, which turns these regional judgments into spatially differentiated policy feedback. It normalizes rewards for each text target across sampled images and casts the resulting regional advantages onto the corresponding latent tokens. Extensive experiments on existing benchmarks and our newly established $\textbf{PolyText-Bench}$ demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in text accuracy and glyph fidelity. Project page: https://sujiehu.github.io/textdart-scanner

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: LICOA: Learning Instruction-Conditioned Optical Actions for Mobile Spatial Augmented Reality
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Yuchen Deng, Shunkai Zhou, Ruixuan Zhu, Haibin Ling, Bingyao Huang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: LICOA enables mobile spatial augmented reality systems to autonomously project light based on language instructions and visual observations, achieving notable success in real-world tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Spatial augmented reality (SAR) augments physical environments with projected content, but most systems assume that the projector pose, target region, or motion path has been fixed or specified. We instead make projected light an embodied action: given a language instruction and current visual observations, a system must decide how to move and where and at what scale to place the projection. We introduce LICOA to realize this capability. Its differential-drive chassis provides room-scale approach and repositioning, while a steerable mirror with two degrees of freedom (2DoF) and projection scale provide rapid local control of the beam. A shared interface maps synchronized external and onboard RGB cameras with robot control state to physical optical actions across pretrained action models. Because instruction-conditioned optical action lacks dedicated training data and a common evaluation protocol, we construct a matched simulation embodiment and a corpus with 150 tasks and 7,500 rendered episodes, then evaluate models trained only on this corpus in previously unseen real-world environments. Across 480 complete closed-loop real-world execution trials (rollouts) on 12 tasks, the best adapted action model achieves a 57.50% success rate and 40.64% success weighted by path length, compared with 8.33% and 5.15% for the same architecture trained from scratch. A further 150 real-world ablation rollouts support the need for both camera views and coordinated control of the chassis and mirror. These results establish a physical platform, shared perception and optical action interface, corpus, and real-world evaluation protocol for treating projected light as an embodied action.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Reinforcement Learning-driven Diffusion Models: Language, Vision, and Beyond
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zhiyuan Ma, Jiabao Wei, Tianyu Wang, Hanqing Wang, Jiadong Pan
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper reviews and analyzes the integration of reinforcement learning into diffusion models, addressing limitations and proposing strategies for improved goal-directed generation across various applications.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have steadily demonstrated outstanding performance in high-fidelity, controllable generation across diverse scenarios, following the "pretraining-finetuning" paradigm established in LLMs. Despite these advances, conventional DMs still face critical limitations in sophisticated reasoning, autonomous exploration of generation pathways, and adaptability to complex, human-aligned objectives. Inspired by RLHF's success in LLMs, RL has recently emerged as a pivotal post-training mechanism to iteratively refine DMs through reward-driven trajectory optimization. This paper presents the first comprehensive review of RL-driven DMs and an empirical analysis of how RL reshapes the diffusion process towards experience-centric, goal-directed generation. We propose a novel technical panorama elucidating RL's multifaceted roles in diffusion-based language, multimodal, robotic, and scientific models, with a granular focus on diffusion trajectory optimization and reward engineering. Through extensive experiments on multiple task-specific benchmarks, we systematically evaluate representative methods to intuitively highlight the advantages of different RL post-training strategies. Furthermore, we reveal and dissect three crucial bottlenecks that currently hinder the real-world deployment of RL-driven DMs: reward design fragility, exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards. Based on these perspectives, we provide a principled roadmap for the integration of RL into DMs and outline promising future research directions for robust, interpretable RL-diffusion systems. We also construct a public repository to continuously track the latest developments in this rapidly evolving field: https://github.com/MAIR-Lab-HUST/Awesome-RL-for-Diffusion-Models.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: HyrCap: Hybrid Rank-Calibration of Action Proposals for Temporal Event Understanding
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Rui Chen, Xingyu Chen, Pengxin Xu, Kai Chen, Junzhi Yu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: HyrCap introduces a hybrid, proposal-centric framework for improving temporal action detection and event understanding in videos by enhancing localization quality and proposal ranking reliability.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Temporal action detection in long untrimmed videos suffers from inaccurate localization and low-quality proposals, especially with sparse annotations and ambiguous boundaries. For open-ended video understanding and LLM-driven event analysis, reliable proposals connect temporal localization, event annotation, and semantic understanding. However, conventional temporal action detection (TAD) pipelines lack explicit modeling of proposal localization quality, cross-representation support, and inter-proposal relations. We propose Hybrid Rank-Calibration of Action Proposals (HyrCap), a proposal-centric query-based TAD framework for temporal event understanding. Hybrid combines complementary video features with different localization cues, while Rank-Calibration adjusts proposal ranking confidence to reflect localization reliability and candidate competition. HyrCap treats dense query-based predictions as an over-complete temporal event hypothesis space. Cross-Representation Consensus Calibration, Localization Quality Estimation, and Proposal Redundancy Suppression improve proposal ranking reliability, localization quality, and candidate discrimination. Inspired by LLMs' capabilities in fine-grained semantic recognition, event description, and reasoning, we introduce HyrCap for Semantic Action Understanding, using calibrated proposals for standard TAD and as inputs to LLM-based semantic understanding. We define a staged evaluation protocol to separately measure event localization, segment-level semantic understanding, and combined event understanding performance. Experiments on public benchmarks show that HyrCap achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple metrics and provides a finer-grained paradigm and evaluation protocol for query-based event segmentation and annotation.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Cracking Mobile Manipulation: From Failure Diagnosis to Agentic Robot System
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zixuan Wang, Jia-Ning Li, Yinzhou Tang, Yanzhao Yu, Biao Wu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper identifies failure points in long-horizon mobile manipulation and presents interventions that significantly enhance task success rates in robotic systems.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong performance on local robot manipulation, yet their success does not readily translate to long-horizon mobile manipulation. In our experiments, a pretrained subtask VLA achieves 80% success rate on atomic manipulation tasks but only 19% when these skills are composed into mobile manipulation. We argue that this gap stems from failures across the execution process rather than from local manipulation capability alone. To uncover these bottlenecks, we systematically diagnose failures in long-horizon mobile manipulation and identify three dominant regimes: task planning, navigation and base positioning, and local manipulation. Based on this diagnosis, we develop failure-guided agentic intervention that augments a fixed subtask VLA with demonstration-based planning guidance, adaptive visual memory, accessibility-aware base adjustment, and local end-effector adjustment. On RoboCasa365, these interventions progressively improve task success from 19% to 47%, with the finalized system reaching 49% on held-out episode seeds, compared with 18% for the baseline. The same design improves performance from 14% to 37% on BEHAVIOR-1K and from 5/20 to 13/20 on real-robot tasks. These results suggest that reliable mobile manipulation can be advanced by diagnosing and intervening on the current bottleneck, rather than uniformly scaling the underlying policy. Our code will be released at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/Cracking-Mobile-Manipulation.git.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: ForceBench: Benchmarking Force Integration for Robotic Manipulation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xuan Han, Zinuo Jin, Tianlin Li, Yunfan Lou, Xin Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: ForceBench is a simulation benchmark that evaluates six-axis wrist-force integration in robotic manipulation, demonstrating significant improvements in task success rates with specific integration designs.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Force feedback provides vision-language-action (VLA) policies with physical observations that can guide action selection and execution. However, differences in tasks, demonstrations, and control settings across existing systems hinder reliable comparisons of force integration designs. We introduce ForceBench, a simulation benchmark for evaluating six-axis wrist-force integration under a unified protocol. ForceBench combines eight tasks spanning physical-property inference, resistance-dependent interaction, and contact-rich assembly with 1,600 synchronized demonstrations and task-specific success criteria. We compare one no-force baseline and six force integration designs on a shared $π_{0.5}$ backbone. Prompt Fusion achieves the highest observed mean simulation success of 35.31%, compared with 23.25% for the baseline, and improves success rates across all three task categories. Predictive and temporal gains in simulation concentrate on physical-property inference, while both temporal designs underperform the baseline on assembly. Real-world evaluation of eight systems across five tasks supports the main qualitative trends: Prompt Fusion and Dual-Path Fusion achieve 63.00% mean success, compared with 40.00% for the baseline, but only Prompt Fusion improves every task. These findings support ForceBench's practical value for identifying the benefits and limitations of force integration across manipulation demands. The project page is available at https://forcebench-platform.github.io/.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: IACM-RL: Intent-Aware Context Management and Reinforcement Learning for Complex Tool Invocation under Dynamic Intent Fluctuations
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Dingwei Zhu, Jiahan Li, Chengjun Pan, Yunxian Yang, Yunbin Zhao
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: IACM-RL introduces a robust framework for tool invocation that effectively manages dynamic user intent fluctuations, outperforming existing methods by minimizing errors and enhancing generalization.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Executing long-horizon tool invocations in real-world environments is severely challenged by dynamic user intent noise. Existing methods attempt robustness via implicit history scanning or text compression, yet predominantly assume perfect instructions in simplistic scenarios. Inevitably, under fluctuating contexts, obsolete constraints dilute model attention, triggering intent deviation and repetitive API loops. To resolve this, we propose IACM-RL, a comprehensive framework for robust tool invocation. First, we introduce the DynamicIntent pipeline, synthesizing trajectories across several fine-grained fluctuation scenarios, paired with a five-dimensional diagnostic metric suite. Second, IACM-RL deploys a BeliefState-based Self-Generated Context Manager that proactively tracks shifting goals and isolates overwritten parameters using structural stale flags. To autonomously internalize this state-tracking capability, we optimize the policy using a hierarchical intent-driven reward alongside two auxiliary losses (CM extraction and state distillation). Experiments on DynamicIntent, BFCL-V3, and $\mathrmτ^2$-Bench demonstrate that IACM-RL outperforms baselines, reducing infinite loops and stale context errors while enhancing out-of-domain generalization.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Interlock: From Local Correctness to Task Completion in Long-Horizon Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Linji Hao, Yanji He, Zihan Wang, Hansi Yang, Jiayuan Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The Interlock framework enhances long-horizon task completion in agents by using a typed completion graph to maintain relationships among tasks, improving performance metrics across various benchmarks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Large language model agents increasingly undertake long-horizon tasks in complex environments characterized by fragmented evidence, partially completed states, and dependencies across resources and artifacts. Existing agents may satisfy individual requirements while failing to maintain these relationships, producing locally correct but incomplete outcomes. These failures arise because task completion depends on relationships among environmental evidence, consequential decisions, and required effects. To address this completion gap, we propose Interlock, a framework for task synthesis that represents each task as a typed completion graph. Grounding edges connect public evidence to decisions, coupling hyperedges impose joint constraints across components, and realization edges connect decisions to all required downstream effects. Interlock compiles this graph into a resettable workspace, a public request, and an evaluation rubric. A source-coverage review checks whether the original requirements survive generation, while a public-input review checks whether the rubric is supported by the materials available to the solver. An agent-as-judge inspects execution artifacts and runs verification scripts, retaining trajectories judged to satisfy all mandatory requirements. To evaluate training utility, we fine-tune two Qwen3.6 backbones on their own accepted trajectories. Across the two backbones, training improves AutomationBench task pass rates by 4.00-4.50 percentage points, JobBench weighted scores by 3.20-6.64 points, and Harvey LAB criterion pass rates by 3.89-4.16 percentage points. These results demonstrate the training utility of the synthesized experience across external task environments.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: C3: Rethinking Process Supervision via Confidence-Guided Credit Correction in Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Ai Jian, Haoran Pan, Eryu Guo, Haojin Yang, Jinghan He
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces Confidence-Guided Credit Correction (C$^3$), enhancing multi-turn reinforcement learning by correcting undesired behaviors while preserving task rewards, improving overall performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Large language models are increasingly trained as multi-turn agents that interact with external tools. However, outcome-only reinforcement learning can produce a form of misguided reinforcement: even on successful trajectories, undesirable local behaviors may receive positive token-level advantages and be favored by the policy update. To address this issue, we propose Confidence-Guided Credit Correction (C$^3$), a plug-in method for local credit correction. C$^3$ identifies spans corresponding to undesirable behaviors and selectively corrects positive credit after advantage estimation, with the correction strength adaptively controlled by the behavior policy's confidence in the corresponding behavior, while leaving the task reward and original credit estimation unchanged. Across multiple multi-turn benchmarks, C$^3$ improves performance under both {critic-based and critic-free reinforcement learning methods}. Injecting the same behavioral signals as turn-level or outcome rewards does not consistently improve performance. Our results show that local credit correction provides an effective form of process supervision for outcome-driven RL.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: PAWA: Panoramic Action-conditioned World Modeling for Multiple Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Siqi Yang, Yimu Wang, Ziqi Cai, Chengxuan Zhu, Shuchen Weng
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: PAWA introduces a novel dataset and framework for action-conditioned panoramic multiplayer world modeling, enhancing POV and panoramic video predictions in shared environments.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: A multiplayer world model must predict how the independent actions of several players change a shared environment, including changes outside a player's current field of view. A point-of-view (POV) video captures such changes only after they enter its field of view, whereas panoramic video records the surroundings in every viewing direction and has served as an intermediate representation of the world state in recent world models. Learning this task therefore requires synchronized POV and panoramic videos of interacting players together with their actions, yet no existing dataset provides this combination in Minecraft, an established testbed in which players act independently in a shared, modifiable 3D world. We present PAWA, a dataset and framework for action-conditioned panoramic multiplayer world modeling. The dataset pairs each player's POV video with world-stabilized panoramic video and aligned actions. Its distributed pipeline decouples CPU gameplay capture from GPU rendering, scales beyond 64 simultaneous players, and re-renders each recorded session under new observation configurations without replaying the gameplay. On this dataset, we develop a dual-tower model that jointly predicts POV and panoramic video and couples the two streams through cross-attention that aligns tokens observing the same direction in a shared world frame. We further introduce a quadratic-phase player encoding that provides many more player codes than existing rotary codes at the same embedding dimension. Experiments show that PAWA outperforms state-of-the-art multiplayer world models in POV prediction quality while also producing high-fidelity panoramic predictions. The dataset and collection pipeline are open source to support further research on multiplayer world models.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Kaifei Wang, Zikang Shan, Liwei Wang, Yinyu Ye, Han Zhong
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper investigates the role of bias-corrected exponential moving average momentum in reinforcement learning, demonstrating that optimal momentum selection enhances performance in policy gradient optimization.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $β$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $β$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $η$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $β$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $β$ to keep $η/(1-β)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base using SGD with EMA and AdamW support our principle of choosing larger coefficients in practical LLM post-training. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $β_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Dual-arm Cooperation for Tabletop Wiping with Temporal Object Removal
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Pengqi Zhang, Longchang Yu, Daohan Li, Liang Yan, Hangxin Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: This paper presents a dual-arm cooperative framework for efficient tabletop wiping by integrating object rearrangement and coverage wiping through a geometry-aware task planner.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: We devise a dual-arm cooperative planning framework for wiping table surface in the presence of scattered objects. Unlike conventional surface-cleaning strategies that only cover free areas and detour around obstacles, our framework explicitly assigns one arm to rearrange objects while the other performs coverage wiping, thereby enabling access to previously obstructed regions. Specifically, we first construct a set of wiping and object-rearrangement action primitives. Based on these primitives, we introduce Geo-MILP, a geometry-aware task planner formulated as Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP). By integrating Logic-Based Benders Decomposition (LBBD), Geo-MILP iteratively optimizes action sequencingand timing to resolve geometric conflicts, promoting efficient cooperation between wiping and object rearrangement. We then employ K-Order Markov Optimization (KOMO) to generate smooth, collision-free motions to ensure feasible execution. Simulation and physical experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework not only increases reachable coverage by enabling access to obstructed areas, but also significantly improves time efficiency compared to Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) baselines, reducing planning time by up to 9 times and execution makespan by approximately 40%.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Decision-Making for Autonomous Driving Guided by Chinese Philosophical Wisdom
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xiaojun Bi, Xiaoyuan Ma, Yiwen Sun, Tianren Huang, Chaoran Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The CPW-Drive framework integrates Chinese philosophical wisdom into autonomous driving decision-making, enhancing safety and efficiency through a retrieval-augmented generation approach, outperforming traditional methods.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Autonomous driving decision systems must balance safety, efficiency, and social norms in complex traffic interactions. Philosophical and ethical considerations have received limited attention in existing autonomous driving decision-making approaches based on numerical optimization, sequence prediction, and large language models (LLMs). We propose Chinese Philosophical Wisdom-Guided Driving (CPW-Drive), a closed-loop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that incorporates value guidance derived from Chinese philosophy into autonomous driving decision-making. Using Chinese Confucian thought as its knowledge source, CPW-Drive consolidates LLM-extracted keywords from relevant classical texts into driving-relevant value principles through manual screening and validation. It then contextualizes these principles through scenario-specific cases to form retrievable and reusable value guidance. We further propose Physics-aware Spatial Similarity Retrieval (PSSR), which compares vehicle layouts and velocity-extrapolated states to retrieve physically relevant historical cases. On Highway-env's multilane highway-driving task, CPW-Drive achieves success rates of 93.0%, 86.0%, and 72.0% across three traffic configurations. These results outperform the strongest baseline by 8.0, 22.5, and 25.0 percentage points, respectively. Across all configurations, CPW-Drive achieves the highest collision-free step count and maintains a low lane-change frequency. The results suggest that structured value guidance can improve simulated closed-loop safety and stability while introducing efficiency and latency trade-offs.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: MemReread: Enhancing Agentic Long-Context Reasoning via Memory-Guided Rereading
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Baibei Ji, Xiaoyang Weng, Juntao Li, Zecheng Tang, Yihang Lou
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: MemReread enhances long-context reasoning by enabling targeted rereading and question decomposition, improving memory efficiency and performance while maintaining linear time complexity.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Long-context reasoning tasks have motivated agent-memory approaches that process document chunks sequentially while maintaining a dynamically updated memory, avoiding the quadratic complexity of standard attention. Existing methods often rely on retrieval to recover information discarded during memory overwriting, but remain vulnerable to evidence loss during memory formation and interference from invalid queries. To overcome these limitations, we propose MemReread. Built upon streaming reading, it circumvents intermediate retrieval, triggering question decomposition and targeted rereading when the final memory is insufficient. By recovering indirect evidence that may have been prematurely discarded, MemReread enables non-linear reasoning while preserving the logical flow of document comprehension. We further introduce a reinforcement learning framework that improves length extrapolation and adaptively determines the number of rereading passes according to task complexity, enabling flexible control of computational overhead. Our MemReread-4B outperforms strong baselines on long-context reasoning tasks (e.g., +1.6pp v.s. DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 2WikiMultiHopQA) while maintaining linear time complexity with respect to context length.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: KineWorld: Action-Induced Transport Fields for Embodied World Modeling
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Ziying Song, Yuchen Liu, Zhuoran Xu, Ziyang Liu, Jian Jin
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: KineWorld introduces a transport-aware framework for embodied world modeling, enhancing action prediction by aligning visual generation with critical spatial changes in robot interactions.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Embodied world models predict the visual consequences of candidate actions before execution. However, existing action-conditioned world models often adopt uniformly weighted visual generation objectives that can be misaligned with embodied prediction needs. Even with explicit motion conditioning, these objectives can underemphasize spatially sparse changes that are critical to interaction. We propose KineWorld, a transport-aware world-modeling framework that extends robot kinematics from motion conditioning to the spatial allocation of generative supervision. Kinematic Transport Lifting (KTL) constructs renderer-derived, camera-aligned transport fields from commanded robot motion. Transport-Aware World Diffusion (TAWD) calibrates their motion support on the video-latent grid and reweights future-RGB flow matching through a normalized mixture of uniform and transport-focused distributions. We train KineWorld using ALOHA-AgileX bimanual manipulation data from RoboTwin 2.0. KineWorld achieves an EWMScore-P of 68.95 in single-view evaluation and a TWB-Score of 54.82 in multi-view evaluation. These results support a shift from appearance fitting toward action-consequence modeling for embodied decision-making.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: What Visual Representations Do World Action Models Need?
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Kai Liu, Jiangran Lyu, Tingyu Deng, Yixin Zheng, Jingtian Wan
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The study identifies that strong general-purpose visual representations enhance World Action Models' manipulation capabilities, outperforming specialized representations, and proposes R$^2$-WAM for improved performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) inherit powerful priors from pretrained video generation models, but their variational autoencoder (VAE) representations are optimized for visual reconstruction rather than manipulation. External visual representations can improve manipulation, but existing methods couple representation choices with different integration mechanisms, obscuring their individual effects. We systematically compare visual representations, five integration mechanisms, and feature combinations under controlled settings. Our study yields three main findings. First, strong general-purpose visual representations provide broader robustness gains and can match or outperform representations pretrained for specific visual capabilities. Second, channel-wise joint prediction achieves the highest average success rate; further analyses suggest that future-feature prediction and the action expert's effective use of added visual information contribute to its gains. Third, additional sources should be selected for the task-relevant information they contribute beyond existing representations, as the same source can help one combination but harm another. However, even the best evaluated composition provides a smaller additional gain than the initial improvement from adding a strong general-purpose representation to the VAE-only baseline. We instantiate the resulting Representation Recipe as R$^2$-WAM. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop with an 84.7% success rate and reaches 92.8% on RoboTwin 2.0, improving over the VAE-only baselines by 5.9 and 2.2 percentage points, respectively. Taken together, these findings suggest that future work should prioritize stronger general-purpose visual representations and more effective mechanisms for integrating them into WAMs, with feature composition serving as a supplementary route to improvement.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: UniMergeTrack: Hierarchical Model Merging for General RGB-X Visual Object Tracking
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Shiao Wang, Xiao Wang, Yuhe Ding, Jiarui Xu, Zikang Yan
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: UniMergeTrack introduces a hierarchical model merging approach for RGB-X visual object tracking, enhancing performance through task-specific optimization and cross-task knowledge integration.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: RGB-X tracking leverages complementary modalities, such as thermal infrared, event, or depth, to improve robustness under challenging conditions. Existing general-purpose RGB-X trackers typically follow two paradigms: independent task-specific training and joint training across modality combinations. However, the former suffers from knowledge isolation and model redundancy, while the latter introduces optimization interference across heterogeneous tasks. In this work, we present UniMergeTrack, a new model merging paradigm that preserves task-specific optimization while enabling effective cross-task knowledge integration. UniMergeTrack first trains modality-specific trackers independently and then performs hierarchical model merging. Specifically, transferable backbones are merged across RGB-X tasks via high-pass-filtered merging, and complemented by lightweight task-specific experts that preserve modality-specific cues. Tracking heads are merged within each task using optimal transport-guided channel alignment to mitigate hidden channel mismatch. A subsequent distribution alignment fine-tuning stage further improves compatibility between the unified backbone and task-specific heads. Extensive experiments on the LasHeR, RGBT234, VisEvent, VOT-RGBD22, COESOT, and CDTB benchmarks demonstrate that UniMergeTrack achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance across RGB-Thermal, RGB-Event, and RGB-Depth tracking tasks, while exhibiting strong generalization to unseen datasets. The source code will be released upon acceptance. The source code of this paper will be released on https://github.com/Event-AHU/OpenEvTracking.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Grounded-Dreamer: Robot Learning from World Model Synthetic Data with Physical Grounding
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Feng Jiang, Shu Chen, Yuanfei Wang, Yuan Li, Zhenhao Shen
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: Grounded-Dreamer synthesizes physically grounded robot manipulation data from real images using video world models, enabling effective policy learning without human demonstrations.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Scaling robot manipulation policies requires large amounts of diverse, action-labeled data, yet collecting such data in the real world remains expensive and difficult to scale. Existing methods either depend on human teleoperation, rely on simulation with limited visual realism, or use human videos that lack embodiment-specific annotations. In this paper, we introduce Grounded-Dreamer, a framework for synthesizing physically grounded robot manipulation data with video world models while avoiding human teleoperation demonstrations. Grounded-Dreamer combines the visual realism of generative video models with simulator physics engines. Starting from a small set of real images depicting robot task initial states, our method automatically reconstructs task-relevant objects and camera geometry, aligns them in simulation, and collects physically valid trajectories. These trajectories are used to post-train both a video world model and an inverse dynamics model, enabling the generation of visually realistic robot manipulation videos and corresponding robot actions from real images. To filter physically implausible rollouts, Grounded-Dreamer replays generated trajectories in the reconstructed simulation and retains only those that successfully complete the tasks. The real-world robot policies are trained solely on the grounded synthetic trajectories without any human demonstrations. Empirical results in real-world tasks demonstrate that Grounded-Dreamer can synthesize physically grounded data and substantially facilitate policy learning without requiring human teleoperation effort.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: AnomalyAgent: Agentic Industrial Anomaly Synthesis via Tool-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiaming Su, Tengchao Yang, Ruikang Zhang, Zhengan Yan, Haoyu Sun
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: AnomalyAgent enhances industrial anomaly synthesis through tool-augmented reinforcement learning, achieving superior performance in generating realistic anomalies and improving classification accuracy.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Industrial anomaly generation is a crucial method for alleviating the data scarcity problem in anomaly detection tasks. Most existing anomaly synthesis methods rely on single-step generation mechanisms, lacking complex reasoning and iterative optimization capabilities, making it difficult to generate anomaly samples with high semantic realism. We propose AnomalyAgent, an anomaly synthesis agent with self-reflection, knowledge retrieval, and iterative refinement capabilities, aiming to generate realistic and diverse anomalies. Specifically, AnomalyAgent is equipped with five tools: Prompt Generation (PG), Image Generation (IG), Quality Evaluation (QE), Knowledge Retrieval (KR), and Mask Generation (MG), enabling closed-loop optimization. To improve decision-making and self-reflection, we construct structured trajectories from real anomaly images and design a two-stage training framework: supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. This process is driven by a three-part reward mechanism: (1) task rewards to supervise the quality and location rationality of generated anomalies; (2) reflection rewards to train the model's ability to improve anomaly synthesis prompt; (3) behavioral rewards to ensure adherence to the trajectory. On the MVTec-AD dataset, AnomalyAgent achieves IS/IC-L of 2.10/0.33 for anomaly generation, 57.0% classification accuracy using ResNet34, and 99.3%/74.2% AP at the image/pixel level using a simple UNet, surpassing all zero-shot SOTA methods. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/sssjmmm/AnomalyAgent.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: OGPO: Offline Goal-conditioned Policy Optimization for Recoverable Vision-Language-Action Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Xule Gao, Xi Wang, Zehua Zang, Rui Wang, Changwen Zheng
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: OGPO enhances offline goal-conditioned policy optimization for vision-language-action models by relabeling trajectories with key states, improving robustness and recoverability in robotic manipulation tasks.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong promise in robotic manipulation, yet their post-training still predominantly relies on trajectory-level supervised imitation over robot demonstrations. While effective for learning feasible actions, this paradigm supervises policies to reproduce expert actions at each step, biasing them toward demonstration-specific action paths and providing limited guidance for recovering toward task-progress states once execution deviates from demonstrated trajectories. To address this limitation, we propose OGPO, an Offline Goal-conditioned Policy Optimization framework for recoverable VLA post-training. Instead of treating offline demonstrations merely as step-wise action labels, OGPO adaptively relabels trajectories with semantic key states and constructs goal-conditioned process rewards to optimize the policy for reaching these task-progress states. In this way, OGPO shifts VLA post-training from trajectory-level action imitation to key-state reachability learning, enabling policies to acquire a more robust ability to complete goal states from feasible off-demonstration states without requiring additional online interaction. Experiments on LIBERO and MetaWorld show that OGPO consistently improves VLA policy performance over standard supervised fine-tuning. Moreover, evaluations on LIBERO-Plus and our proposed LIBERO-ReAct, a mid-execution perturbation benchmark, further demonstrate that OGPO achieves stronger robustness and goal-directed recoverability under distribution shifts and recoverable off-demonstration states.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: EmbodiedCLBench: Evaluating Continual Learning for Self-Evolving Embodied Agents
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jie Huang, Yanan Chen, Ruixun Liu, Kaichen He, Xinyi He
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: EmbodiedCLBench is a novel benchmark for assessing continual learning in self-evolving agents within embodied environments, revealing limitations and insights into skill transfer and task complexity.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Continual learning requires models to accumulate past experience and transfer it to new tasks. Despite substantial research on continual learning, existing work remains largely confined to non-embodied settings, without extending to embodied environments. To address this gap, we introduce EmbodiedCLBench, the first benchmark in embodied simulation for evaluating the continual learning capability of self-evolving agents. With compositional generalization as the core evaluation principle, our benchmark evaluates whether agents can first learn from basic tasks and then recombine the acquired skills to solve complex, unseen advanced tasks. Based on EmbodiedCLBench, we conduct extensive experiments across multiple agent harnesses and learning methods, revealing consistent limitations and distinctive behaviors. Our results show that while advanced tasks can be hardly solved under zero-shot setting, the experience from basic tasks enables consistent improvement. Such benefit from the experience remains stable even if the task complexity increases. However, this improvement does not scale accordingly with the number of learning samples, and current agents cannot extract meaningful information from additional experience. Collectively, our findings highlight continual learning as a fundamental yet underexplored capability, and our benchmark offers valuable resources for designing effective self-evolving agents in embodied environments. Our code and dataset are available at https://pku-value-lab.github.io/EmbodiedCLBench-homepage.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: HENet++: Hybrid Encoding and Multi-task Learning for 3D Perception and End-to-end Autonomous Driving
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zhongyu Xia, Zhiwei Lin, Yongtao Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: HENet++ is a unified multi-task framework for 3D perception in autonomous driving, optimizing accuracy and efficiency through hybrid image encoding and task-specific feature extraction.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Three-dimensional feature extraction and multi-task perception are fundamental components of modern autonomous driving systems. Although large image encoders, high-resolution inputs, and long temporal contexts can substantially improve representation quality and overall performance, jointly leveraging these strategies remains challenging due to prohibitive computational costs during both training and inference. Furthermore, different perception tasks often require distinct feature representations, making it difficult for a unified architecture to achieve end-to-end multi-task performance comparable to specialized single-task systems. To address these challenges, we propose HENet++, a unified framework for multi-task 3D perception and end-to-end autonomous driving that employs a hybrid image encoding strategy, using a large encoder for short-term frames and a lightweight encoder for long-term temporal context to strike a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency. The framework jointly extracts dense background features and sparse foreground features, enabling task-specific representations that reduce cumulative errors and provide richer information for downstream prediction and planning modules. HENet++ is compatible with diverse 3D feature extraction pipelines and supports multi-modal inputs, including camera and radar data. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on the nuScenes multi-task 3D perception benchmark, achieving the lowest collision rate on the nuScenes planning benchmark and higher PDMS on the NAVSIM benchmark.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: EagleVLA: Towards Onboard Real-Time Robot Control via Foresight-Aligned Asynchronous Inference
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zebin Yang, Qi Wang, Yunhe Wang, Xiurui Guo, Bo Yu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: EagleVLA enhances onboard Vision-Language-Action model performance through foresight-aligned asynchronous inference, achieving significant improvements in control frequency and success rate on low-power devices.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have achieved impressive performance on diverse embodied tasks. However, deploying VLA models on low-power onboard devices, such as the Jetson Orin, remains challenging due to their high computational complexity, which leads to substantial inference latency and low control frequency. Asynchronous inference can partially mask this latency by parallelizing action execution and subsequent inference, but it introduces two critical issues: perception-execution misalignment and long reaction time. In this paper, we propose EagleVLA, a method for efficient VLA deployment on onboard devices via Foresight-Aligned Asynchronous Correction. To address misalignment, we train a lightweight future correction module that predicts future environment representations, allowing the action expert to predict actions from the future time step. To reduce reaction time, we introduce confidence-based scheduling optimization that adaptively balances VLM and action expert invocations. We also build a llama.cpp-based inference engine tailored for onboard VLA deployment, with system-level optimizations including CUDA graph reuse, GPU-resident intermediate buffering, and flow unrolling. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EagleVLA achieves 9.85x and 6.19x improvements in control frequency compared with naive PyTorch and vla.cpp on Jetson Orin, while outperforming VLASH by 14.8% in success rate on LIBERO benchmark. The code of our asynchronous algorithm is available on https://github.com/PKU-SEC-Lab/EagleVLA, and our efficient llama.cpp-based inference engine is available on https://github.com/PKU-SEC-Lab/EagleVLA-Edge.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: MemoWM: How World Models Change What Agents Need to Remember
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Bingfan Zeng, Zhisheng Chen, Chenbo Sang, Zhengwei Xie, Jinpeng Wang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: MemoWM is a framework that optimizes memory allocation for long-term agents by using world models to compress information, achieving higher accuracy and reduced storage needs.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Long-term agents face growing storage demands as they accumulate experience. World models capture reusable regularities that can reduce the information stored for each experience. We formulate the problem of memory allocation conditioned on a world model and introduce MemoWM, a framework that uses shared predictions to compress retained information and reconstruct omitted content. Its task-aware allocation rule balances the expected impact of reconstruction errors against storage cost, retaining information with downstream value beyond the predictive prior. Across five long-term agent-memory benchmarks, MemoWM achieves 42.42\% average answer accuracy, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.62 percentage points, while reducing average experience-specific storage by 53.9\% relative to MIRIX, the most storage-efficient baseline. Further analysis shows that stronger world models reduce per-experience storage at comparable task quality. Accounting for model parameters reveals a trade-off between shared model capacity and recurring storage costs, with the capacity that minimizes total storage increasing as more interactions are retained. Our code is available at https://github.com/Feld-maxiu/MemoWM.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: SPAN-Nav: Generalized Spatial Awareness for Versatile Embodied Navigation
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Jiahang Liu, Tianyu Xu, Jiawei Chen, Lu Yue, Jiazhao Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: SPAN-Nav is a novel end-to-end model enhancing embodied navigation with universal 3D spatial awareness through compact spatial priors and multi-task co-training, achieving state-of-the-art performance.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Recent embodied navigation approaches leveraging Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate strong generalization in versatile Vision-Language Navigation (VLN). However, reliable path planning in complex environments remains challenging due to insufficient spatial awareness. In this work, we introduce SPAN-Nav, an end-to-end foundation model designed to infuse embodied navigation with universal 3D spatial awareness using RGB video streams. SPAN-Nav extracts spatial priors across diverse scenes through an occupancy prediction task on extensive indoor and outdoor environments. To mitigate the computational burden, we introduce a compact representation for spatial priors, finding that a single token is sufficient to encapsulate the coarse-grained cues essential for navigation tasks. Furthermore, inspired by the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) mechanism, SPAN-Nav utilizes this single spatial token to explicitly inject spatial cues into action reasoning through an end-to end framework. Leveraging multi-task co-training, SPAN-Nav captures task-adaptive cues from generalized spatial priors, enabling robust spatial awareness to generalize even to the task lacking explicit spatial supervision. To support comprehensive spatial learning, we present a massive dataset of 4.2 million occupancy annotations that covers both indoor and outdoor scenes across multi-type navigation tasks. SPAN-Nav achieves state-of-the-art performance across three benchmarks spanning diverse scenarios and varied navigation tasks. Finally, real-world experiments validate the robust generalization and practical reliability of our approach across complex physical scenarios.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: World-Ego Modeling for Embodied Video Generation in Long-Horizon Navigation-Manipulation Tasks
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Zuyao Lin, Jianhui Zhang, Peidong Jia, Xiaoguang Zhao, Shanghang Zhang
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces the World-Ego Model (WEM) for disentangled embodied video generation, enhancing long-horizon navigation-manipulation tasks through a novel vision-language state predictor and dataset.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Embodied video world models typically capture both scene evolution and the robot's behavior, which we refer to as the \emph{world} and the \emph{ego}, respectively. The world and the ego exhibit different underlying dynamics: world prediction relies primarily on visual history and emphasizes scene stability, whereas ego prediction relies more strongly on the current instruction and emphasizes accurate instruction following. Modeling both components within a single generation stream can entangle these different dependencies, making it difficult to specialize the prediction of either component. Consequently, it becomes difficult to simultaneously maintain scene consistency and accurate instruction following, particularly in long-horizon navigation-manipulation tasks. In this paper, we propose to decompose an embodied video into the world and the ego and disentangle their generation processes. Specifically, we define the world as the background and currently unmanipulated objects, and the ego as the robot and currently manipulated objects. Based on this definition, we develop the \emph{World-Ego Model} (WEM), which combines a vision-language state predictor using role-conditioned attention (RCA) and asymmetric query budgets with a semantic-routed mixture-of-experts (SR-MoE) diffusion generator. To enable rigorous evaluation, we further construct HTEWorld, a dataset and benchmark for long-horizon embodied video generation with hybrid navigation-manipulation tasks, providing 125K training video clips comprising over 4.5M frames with fine-grained instructions, together with 300 multi-turn evaluation trajectories covering over 2K instructions. Extensive experiments show that WEM achieves state-of-the-art performance on HTEWorld while remaining competitive on existing manipulation-oriented evaluations.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Deconstructing Off-Policy Ratios: Entropy-Normalized Trust Regions for Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: Guanqun Zhao, Zijun Xie, Binbin Zheng, Yehan Yang, Jiafeng Lu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces Entropy-Normalized Trust Regions (ENTR) to enhance asynchronous reinforcement learning by stabilizing optimization and improving performance through entropy-aware off-policy ratio management.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) accelerates large language model (LLM) post-training by overlapping rollout generation with policy optimization, but the resulting stale, off-policy data destabilizes optimization and can cause policy collapse. Existing methods gate tokens by ratio magnitude alone, applying one threshold at every position. We show that the ratio's natural scale is set by token entropy, so deviations from mid-trajectory weight updates stay within this scale and carry genuine exploration. We further identify an overlooked low-entropy regime that breaks this scaling, where a near-zero probability amplifies train--inference mismatch into noise far beyond what the local entropy admits. A magnitude threshold admits this noise and discards the exploration. We therefore propose the Entropy-Normalized Trust Region (ENTR). Across long-horizon agentic tasks and mathematical reasoning benchmarks, ENTR outperforms existing asynchronous methods. It improves avg@1 on BrowseComp-Plus by $6.9\%$ over the strongest baseline, trains stably up to $30$ policy versions of staleness, and matches synchronous GRPO at a $2.6\times$ speedup.

情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).title: Learning to Retrieve: Internalizing Memory Retrieval for Video World Models
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).authors_text: JiaKui Hu, Tailai Chen, Yuqi Pan, Xuerui Qiu, Jialun Liu
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).summary: The paper introduces Learning-to-Retrieve (L2R), which internalizes memory retrieval in video world models to enhance long-term scene consistency without relying on external memory systems.
情感与认知智能机器人实验室 (ACIR).debug_abstract: Video world models aim to generate explorable, 3D-consistent scene videos conditioned on camera trajectories.
